requirements.text: In case the 77 GHz radar module (an ESA which is an intentional RF transmitter) has not received type approval in conjunction with a vehicle manufacturer, the radar module shall be supplied with suitable installation guidelines.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the delivery documentation of the radar module for installation guidelines covering mounting, wiring and antenna/transmitter installation conditions.

requirements.text: For ESA type approval, the representative radar module and front camera module shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 6 of UN R10 (configurations other than REESS charging mode).
requirements.test_case: Review the ESA test reports showing compliance with paragraphs 6.5 to 6.9 (radiated emissions, radiated immunity and conducted transients, where applicable) for each module.

requirements.text: An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every ESA (77 GHz radar module and front camera module) conforming to a type approved under UN R10. Per paragraph 5.5, the marking need not be visible when the ESA is installed in the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Inspect production samples of the radar and camera modules for the presence of the UN R10 approval mark on the housing or label.

requirements.text: The ESA approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the mark on the module label for a circle enclosing "E" and the correct country distinguishing number.

requirements.text: The ESA approval mark shall include, to the right of the circle, the number of this Regulation (10), followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module label to check that "10R-" followed by the granted approval number appears to the right of the E-circle.

requirements.text: The radar module and the front camera module (ESAs), with their connections and wiring, shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN R10.
requirements.test_case: Review the ESA design, installation instructions and the full R10 ESA test report set for completeness.

requirements.text: The radar module and the front camera module shall be tested for radiated emissions, conducted emissions, immunity to radiated disturbances and immunity to conducted disturbances.
requirements.test_case: Check that test reports exist for Annex 7, Annex 8, Annex 9 and Annex 10 tests for each module.

requirements.text: When measured using the method of Annex 7, the broadband radiated emission of the ESA shall not exceed 62 to 52 dB µV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band (decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz), 52 to 63 dB µV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band (increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz) and 63 dB µV/m constant in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: Measure broadband radiated emissions of each module per Annex 7 (ALSE, 30–1,000 MHz) and compare with the Appendix 6 limit line.

requirements.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband emission values, expressed in dB µV/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Verify that all Annex 7 readings for both modules are below the limit line.

requirements.text: When measured using the method of Annex 8, the narrowband radiated emission of the ESA shall not exceed 52 to 42 dB µV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band (decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz), 42 to 53 dB µV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band (increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz) and 53 dB µV/m constant in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: Measure narrowband emissions per Annex 8 with an average detector and compare with the Appendix 7 limit line.

requirements.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband emission value, expressed in dB µV/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Verify that all Annex 8 readings for both modules are below the limit line.

requirements.text: In case the module is supplied from 12 V or 24 V supply lines, the emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on the 12/24 V supply lines, tested according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10, shall not exceed the maximum allowed pulse amplitudes of Table 1: for a 12 V system +75 V positive and -100 V negative; for a 24 V system +150 V positive and -450 V negative.
requirements.test_case: Measure switching transients on the module supply line per ISO 7637-2 and compare the peak amplitudes with Table 1.

requirements.text: The immunity of the ESA to electromagnetic radiation, tested by the Annex 9 method(s), shall be demonstrated at the test levels of Table 2a in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band and at not less than the minimum test levels of Table 2b over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: Perform radiated immunity tests per Annex 9 with the selected method(s) and confirm the applied levels against Tables 2a/2b.

requirements.text: Test level in over 90 per cent of the band: Stripline 60 V/m (20–400 MHz); TEM cell 75 V/m (20–200 MHz); BCI 60 mA (20–400 MHz); ALSE 30 V/m (80–2,000 MHz) and 10 V/m (2,000–6,000 MHz); reverberation chamber 21 V/m (LUF–2,000 MHz) and 7 V/m (2,000–6,000 MHz).
requirements.test_case: Check the calibrated field or current levels per frequency range in the immunity test report.

requirements.text: Minimum test level over the whole band: Stripline 50 V/m (20–400 MHz); TEM cell 62.5 V/m (20–200 MHz); BCI 50 mA (20–400 MHz); ALSE 25 V/m (80–2,000 MHz) and 8 V/m (2,000–6,000 MHz); reverberation chamber 18 V/m (LUF–2,000 MHz) and 6 V/m (2,000–6,000 MHz).
requirements.test_case: Verify that no test frequency was applied below the Table 2b minimum level.

requirements.text: During the radiated immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, there shall be no degradation of performance of the immunity related functions of the radar module and the front camera module (e.g. object detection for ACC/AEB/collision warning, lane detection, traffic-sign recognition).
requirements.test_case: Monitor the sensor outputs (object list, lane/sign data, bus messages, fault flags) during Annex 9 exposure and check for no degradation.

requirements.text: In case the module is supplied from 12 V or 24 V supply lines, the immunity of the ESA to transient disturbances conducted along the supply lines shall be demonstrated according to ISO 16750-2 (starting profile) and ISO 7637-2 (pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b) as described in Annex 10, at the test levels of Tables 3a and 3b and with the required functional status classification.
requirements.test_case: Apply the starting profile and ISO 7637-2 pulses to the module supply line and evaluate functional status per ISO 16750-1 / ISO 7637-1.

requirements.text: Starting profile (applicable where the ESA could be installed in vehicles with an ICE started by a 12 V/24 V starter motor): immunity test level II for 12 V and 24 V systems, 10 pulses; functional status class B for ESA related to immunity related functions that shall be operational during engine start phases, class C for other ESA related to immunity related functions, and class D for ESA not related to immunity related functions.
requirements.test_case: Apply 10 ISO 16750-2 starting profile pulses at level II and classify the module behaviour per ISO 16750-1.

requirements.text: Transient pulse immunity (in case of actuating or other immunity related functions / in case of no immunity related functions): pulse 1 at -75 V (12 V) or -450 V (24 V), 500 pulses, FPSC III / III; pulse 2a at +37 V (12 V and 24 V), 500 pulses, FPSC I / III; pulse 2b at +10 V (12 V) or +20 V (24 V), 10 pulses, FPSC II / III; pulse 3a at -112 V (12 V) or -150 V (24 V), 1 h, FPSC I / III; pulse 3b at +75 V (12 V) or +150 V (24 V), 1 h, FPSC I / III.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b at the specified levels and durations and verify the achieved FPSC.

requirements.text: In case the module has no immunity related functions (e.g. pure information functions not classified as immunity related), it need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and is deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8 and Annex 9.
requirements.test_case: Review the function classification of each module against the definition of immunity related functions.

requirements.text: In case the module is not switched, contains no switches and includes no inductive load, it need not be tested for transient conducted emission and is deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
requirements.test_case: Review the module schematic for switches and inductive loads on the supply input.

requirements.text: Loss of function of the radar receiver during the immunity test, when the test signal is within the receiver bandwidth (RF exclusion band) specified for the radio service in the harmonized international EMC standard, does not necessarily lead to a fail criterion.
requirements.test_case: Identify the radar RF exclusion band in the test plan and evaluate any loss of function inside it separately.

requirements.text: The 77 GHz radar module, as an RF transmitter, shall be tested in transmit mode during the emission and immunity tests.
requirements.test_case: Confirm in the test report that the radar was transmitting during the Annex 7/8/9 tests.

requirements.text: Spurious emissions of the radar module (harmonics, parasitic emissions, intermodulation and frequency conversion products outside the necessary bandwidth) shall meet the R10 emission limits; wanted emissions within the necessary bandwidth and out-of-band emissions are disregarded.
requirements.test_case: Assess radiated emissions in 30–1,000 MHz with the radar transmitting and check that spurious products are below the Annex 7/8 limits.

requirements.text: The radar module and the front camera module approved as ESAs under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraph 6.
requirements.test_case: Take production samples of each module and repeat the paragraph 6 ESA emission, immunity and, where applicable, transient tests against the approved type data.

requirements.text: When an ESA (radar module or front camera module) taken from the series is verified, its measured broadband electromagnetic disturbance levels shall not exceed by more than 4 dB (60 per cent) the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.5.2.1.
requirements.test_case: Measure broadband radiated emissions of a series sample per Annex 7 and check that no value exceeds the 6.5.2.1 limit by more than 4 dB.

requirements.text: When an ESA (radar module or front camera module) taken from the series is verified, its measured narrowband electromagnetic disturbance levels shall not exceed by more than 4 dB (60 per cent) the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.6.2.1. In case the radar transmitter's in-band emission is excluded under the exceptions, only its out-of-band emissions are assessed. In case the radar is operated in a non-transmitting test mode, the module is measured in that mode.
requirements.test_case: Measure narrowband radiated emissions of a series sample per Annex 8 and check that no value exceeds the 6.6.2.1 limit by more than 4 dB.

requirements.text: When an ESA (radar module or front camera module) taken from the series is verified for immunity to electromagnetic radiation, it shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle that could be observed by the driver or other road users when subjected to test levels up to 80 per cent of the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.8.2.1.
requirements.test_case: Perform the Annex 9 radiated immunity test on a series sample at 80 % of the 6.8.2.1 levels while monitoring ACC/collision warning and lane-keeping outputs for degradation.

requirements.text: In case the radar or camera module is supplied from 12 V or 24 V supply lines, the component or STU taken from the series shall show no degradation of performance of immunity related functions up to the conducted transient test levels given in paragraph 6.9.1.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 7637-2 test pulses of paragraph 6.9.1 to the supply lines of a series sample and verify the required functional performance status of the immunity related functions.

requirements.text: In case the radar or camera module is supplied from 12 V or 24 V supply lines, the component or STU taken from the series shall not exceed the conducted transient emission levels given in paragraph 6.7.1.
requirements.test_case: Measure the conducted transient emissions of a series sample on its supply lines per ISO 7637-2 (Annex 10) and compare the pulse amplitudes with the 6.7.1 limits.

requirements.text: The ESA broadband emission limits of paragraph 6.5 shall be met throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
requirements.test_case: Scan radiated broadband emissions from 30 to 1,000 MHz in horizontal and vertical polarisation and compare them with the paragraph 6.5 limits.

requirements.text: The ESA broadband emission limits apply to quasi-peak detector readings; if peak detectors are used, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied when assessing compliance.
requirements.test_case: Confirm that quasi-peak readings, or peak readings corrected by 20 dB, are below the paragraph 6.5 limits across 30–1,000 MHz.

requirements.text: The narrowband emission limits of paragraph 6.6.2.1 shall be met by the ESA throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz when measured in an ALSE or OATS.
requirements.test_case: Perform an ALSE scan per CISPR 25 from 30 to 1,000 MHz in horizontal and vertical polarisation and compare the readings with the 6.6.2.1 limits.

requirements.text: Compliance of the ESA with the narrowband emission limits shall be determined from measurements made with an average detector.
requirements.test_case: Verify in the test report that the emission readings compared against the limits were taken with an average detector.

requirements.text: The radar module and the front camera module (ESAs) shall comply with the radiated immunity requirements using any combination, chosen by the manufacturer, of the absorber chamber test (ISO 11452-2), TEM cell test (ISO 11452-3), bulk current injection test (ISO 11452-4), stripline test (ISO 11452-5) and reverberation chamber test (ISO 11452-11), provided the combination covers the full frequency range of 20 to 6,000 MHz.
requirements.test_case: Review the immunity test plan and reports to confirm that the selected ISO 11452 methods together cover 20 to 6,000 MHz without gaps.

requirements.text: The ESA (radar module and camera module) shall be exposed to the immunity test signal over the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range, with frequency steps and dwell times according to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Verify in the test report that the swept frequency range spans 20 to 6,000 MHz with ISO 11452-1 step sizes and dwell times.

requirements.text: In the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, the immunity test signal applied to the ESA shall be amplitude modulated (AM) with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth.
requirements.test_case: Check the signal generator settings in the test report for AM, 1 kHz, 80 % depth between 20 and 400 MHz.

requirements.text: In the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, the immunity test signal applied to the ESA shall be pulse modulated type PM2 with Ton 3 µs and period 3,333 µs.
requirements.test_case: Check the signal generator settings in the test report for PM2 (Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs) between 2,700 and 3,100 MHz.

requirements.text: In the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, the immunity test signal applied to the ESA shall be pulse modulated type PM3 with Ton 500 µs and period 1,000 µs.
requirements.test_case: Check the signal generator settings in the test report for PM3 (Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs) in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz bands.

requirements.text: In case the radar module or front camera module is supplied from 12 V or 24 V supply lines, the ESA shall be immune to the test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 applied to its supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b to the module supply lines and check the functional status against the criteria of paragraph 6.8/6.9.

requirements.text: In case the radar module or front camera module has other connections which may be operationally connected to the 12/24 V supply lines (e.g. ignition/wake-up lines), the ESA shall be immune to the test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 applied to those connections.
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b to each connection that can be operationally connected to the supply lines and verify module behaviour.

requirements.text: In case the radar module or front camera module is supplied from 12 V or 24 V supply lines and is not exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles without a 12 V/24 V starter motor, the ESA shall be immune to the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 applied to its supply lines and to other connections which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 16750-2 starting profile to the supply and related lines and verify module behaviour during and after the profile.

requirements.text: In case the radar module or front camera module is supplied from 12 V or 24 V supply lines, the transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on its supply lines, measured according to ISO 7637-2, shall be limited (in line with paragraph 6.9).
requirements.test_case: Measure the transient emissions on the module supply lines according to ISO 7637-2 and compare them with the applicable limits.

requirements.text: In case the radar module or front camera module has other connections which may be operationally connected to the 12/24 V supply lines, the transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on those connections, measured according to ISO 7637-2, shall be limited.
requirements.test_case: Measure the transient emissions according to ISO 7637-2 on each connection that can be operationally connected to the supply lines.

requirements.text: In case the radar module or front camera module has other connections which may be operationally connected to the 12/24 V supply lines (e.g. ignition/wake-up lines) and is not exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles without a 12 V/24 V starter motor, the ESA shall be immune to the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 applied to those connections.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 16750-2 starting profile to each connection that can be operationally connected to the supply lines, and verify the ESA's functional status meets the immunity criteria.

requirements.text: In case the lower bumper height at the test position is less than 425 mm, the bumper shall meet the flexible lower legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 5.1.1.
requirements.test_case: Measure the lower bumper reference line height at the test positions on the vehicle in its normal ride attitude and confirm the flexible lower legform test is applied.

requirements.text: In case the lower bumper height at the test position is greater than or equal to 425 mm and less than 500 mm, the bumper shall meet either the flexible lower legform requirements of paragraph 5.1.1. or the upper legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 5.1.2., at the choice of the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Measure the lower bumper height and check that the test chosen by the manufacturer (lower or upper legform) is documented and passed.

requirements.text: In case the lower bumper height at the test position is greater than or equal to 500 mm, the bumper shall meet the upper legform to bumper requirements of paragraph 5.1.2.
requirements.test_case: Measure the lower bumper height and confirm the upper legform to bumper test is applied.

requirements.text: When the bumper is tested with the flexible lower legform impactor in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1., the absolute value of the maximum dynamic medial collateral ligament elongation at the knee shall not exceed 22 mm.
requirements.test_case: Perform flexible lower legform impacts at the selected points in the bumper test area and check that peak MCL elongation is ≤ 22 mm.

requirements.text: When the bumper is tested with the flexible lower legform impactor in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1., the maximum dynamic anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament elongation shall not exceed 13 mm.
requirements.test_case: Perform flexible lower legform impacts in the bumper test area and check that peak ACL and PCL elongations are each ≤ 13 mm.

requirements.text: When the bumper is tested with the flexible lower legform impactor in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 1., the absolute value of the dynamic bending moments at the tibia shall not exceed 340 Nm.
requirements.test_case: Perform flexible lower legform impacts and check that the peak absolute tibia bending moments at all tibia gauges are ≤ 340 Nm.

requirements.text: In case the manufacturer nominates relaxation bumper test widths (maximum 264 mm in total), the absolute value of the tibia bending moment within those widths shall not exceed 380 Nm.
requirements.test_case: Check that the nominated relaxation widths total ≤ 264 mm and that lower legform impacts within them give tibia bending moments ≤ 380 Nm.

requirements.text: In case the upper legform to bumper test applies, when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 2., the instantaneous sum of the impact forces with respect to time shall not exceed 7.5 kN.
requirements.test_case: Perform upper legform to bumper impacts and check that the peak summed impactor force is ≤ 7.5 kN.

requirements.text: In case the upper legform to bumper test applies, when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraph 2., the bending moment on the test impactor shall not exceed 510 Nm.
requirements.test_case: Perform upper legform to bumper impacts and check that the peak bending moments at all impactor gauges are ≤ 510 Nm.

requirements.text: In case the fascia top forms part of the bonnet leading edge or extends into the headform test area, when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3., 4. and 5., the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the combined bonnet top test area and windscreen test area.
requirements.test_case: Perform child and adult headform impacts over the test grid, including points on the fascia, and check that HIC ≤ 1,000 over at least two thirds of the combined area.

requirements.text: In case the fascia top forms part of the bonnet leading edge or extends into the headform test area, the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the bonnet top test area.
requirements.test_case: Evaluate the headform test results within the bonnet top test area and verify that HIC ≤ 1,000 over at least two thirds of it.

requirements.text: In case the fascia top forms part of the bonnet leading edge or extends into the headform test area, the HIC for the remaining test areas shall not exceed 1,700 for both headforms.
requirements.test_case: Perform headform impacts on the fascia points in the test area and check that HIC ≤ 1,700 everywhere outside the HIC 1,000 zone.

requirements.text: In case there is only a child headform test area and the fascia extends into it, the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over two thirds of the test area, and shall not exceed 1,700 over the remaining area.
requirements.test_case: Perform child headform impacts over the test area and verify HIC ≤ 1,000 over at least two thirds of it and HIC ≤ 1,700 elsewhere.

requirements.text: In case the fascia extends into the child headform test area, when tested in accordance with Annex 5, paragraphs 3. and 4., the HIC recorded shall not exceed 1,000 over a minimum of one half of the child headform test area.
requirements.test_case: Perform child headform impacts and verify that HIC ≤ 1,000 over at least half of the child headform test area.

requirements.text: In case the fascia extends into the child headform test area, the child headform HIC for the remaining areas shall not exceed 1,700.
requirements.test_case: Check that child headform impacts on the fascia points outside the HIC 1,000 zone give HIC ≤ 1,700.

requirements.text: A vehicle approved pursuant to UN R127 shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the pedestrian safety requirements of paragraph 5 (lower legform or upper legform to bumper test and headform tests, as applicable).
requirements.test_case: Take production bumper systems fitted to production vehicles and repeat selected flexible lower legform (or upper legform) impacts in the bumper test area, checking that the results still meet the paragraph 5 limits and match the approved type's design specification.

requirements.text: At the time of testing, the vehicle or sub-system (front bumper system) shall have a relative humidity of 40 per cent ± 30 per cent and a stabilized temperature of 20 °C ± 4 °C, and the pedestrian protection performance shall be achieved under these conditions.
requirements.test_case: Log the humidity and temperature of the conditioned vehicle or sub-system before each impact and confirm they are within 40 ± 30 % RH and 20 ± 4 °C.

requirements.text: For the pedestrian impact tests, the vehicle carrying the bumper system shall be in its normal ride attitude.
requirements.test_case: Measure the vehicle ride height at the reference points before testing and compare it with the manufacturer's normal ride attitude.

requirements.text: Where a cut-body is used, the cut-body shall include all parts of the vehicle front structure, including the complete bumper system (fascia, absorber, pedestrian foam, beam, brackets and attached sensor modules), all under-bonnet components and all components behind the windscreen that may be involved in a frontal impact with a vulnerable road user.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the cut-body against the vehicle build list to confirm all bumper components and attachments are present and mounted as in series production.

requirements.text: In case the bumper system includes an active pedestrian protection device, that device shall be correctly activated before, and/or be active during, the relevant pedestrian impact test.
requirements.test_case: Verify the activation state of the active device at the moment of impact, using high-speed video and the device's status signals.

requirements.text: Where bumper system components (e.g. movable sensor covers, active grille shutters or adjustable parts), other than active pedestrian protection devices, can change shape or position and have more than one fixed shape or position, the vehicle shall comply with the pedestrian protection requirements with the components in each fixed shape or position.
requirements.test_case: Identify all fixed positions of the movable components and perform or justify the legform/headform impacts in each position.

requirements.text: The peak tibia bending moments and knee ligament elongations of the flexible lower legform impactor used to assess the bumper shall be determined only within the assessment interval (AI) defined in paragraph 2.2 of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: In the lower legform to bumper test, evaluate the peak tibia bending moments and ligament elongations only within the AI computed from the bone segment zero crossings, and compare them with the limits.

requirements.text: In case of the flexible lower legform test (lower bumper reference line below 425 mm, or 425–500 mm at the manufacturer's choice), the measuring points for the lower legform to bumper tests shall be in the bumper test area as defined in paragraph 2.14.
requirements.test_case: Mark the bumper test area (corners of bumper or beam ends minus 42 mm) on the vehicle and check that all selected impact points lie within it.

requirements.text: In case of the flexible lower legform test, the bumper shall meet the lower legform requirements at a minimum of three test positions, one each in the middle and the outer thirds of the bumper test area, at the positions judged most likely to cause injury.
requirements.test_case: Perform lower legform impacts in the middle and both outer thirds at the stiffest or most injurious locations and evaluate the results against para. 5.1.1.

requirements.text: In case of the flexible lower legform test, where the type of structure varies across the bumper test area (e.g. radar module, beam ends, brackets), the bumper shall meet the requirements at test points on different types of structure, spaced at least 84 mm apart horizontally and perpendicular to the longitudinal median plane.
requirements.test_case: Select impact points on each distinct structure type, at least 84 mm apart laterally, and verify compliance at each point.

requirements.text: In case of the flexible lower legform test, the bumper shall be impacted with the impact velocity vector in the horizontal plane and parallel to the longitudinal vertical plane of the vehicle (±2° at first contact), with the impactor axis vertical (roll and pitch ±2°).
requirements.test_case: Check the impactor direction and attitude at first contact using high-speed video or launcher alignment records during the lower legform tests.

requirements.text: In case of the flexible lower legform test, the bumper shall be impacted with the bottom of the impactor at 75 mm ± 10 mm above the ground reference plane at the time of first contact.
requirements.test_case: Measure the impactor bottom height at first contact from high-speed video and the launcher setup.

requirements.text: In case of the flexible lower legform test, the impactor shall strike the bumper with the intended orientation about its vertical axis, with a yaw tolerance of ±5° at first contact.
requirements.test_case: Verify the impactor yaw angle at first contact from video or launcher alignment.

requirements.text: In case of the flexible lower legform test, the bumper shall be impacted at the selected measuring points within a horizontal and vertical impact tolerance of ±10 mm.
requirements.test_case: Measure the actual impact location against the target point using markers or video.

requirements.text: In case of the flexible lower legform test, the bumper shall be impacted by the lower legform at an impact velocity of 11.1 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.
requirements.test_case: Measure the impactor velocity just before first contact, corrected for gravity, and confirm 10.9–11.3 m/s.

requirements.text: In case of the upper legform to bumper test (lower bumper reference line above 500 mm, or 425–500 mm at the manufacturer's choice), the measuring points shall be in the bumper test area as defined in paragraph 2.14.
requirements.test_case: Mark the bumper test area on the vehicle and check that the upper legform impact points lie within it.

requirements.text: In case of the upper legform to bumper test, the bumper shall meet the requirements at a minimum of three test positions, one each in the middle and the outer thirds of the bumper test area, at the positions most likely to cause injury, on different types of structure, at least 84 mm apart horizontally.
requirements.test_case: Perform upper legform impacts in each third at the worst-case structures and evaluate them against para. 5.1.2.

requirements.text: In case of the upper legform to bumper test, the bumper shall be impacted parallel to the vehicle longitudinal axis (±2°) with the upper legform axis vertical, and with the impactor centre line vertically midway between the upper and lower bumper reference lines (±10 mm) and laterally at the selected location (±10 mm).
requirements.test_case: Determine the UBRL and LBRL on the vehicle, set the impactor at their midpoint, and verify the alignment at first contact.

requirements.text: In case of the upper legform to bumper test, the bumper shall be impacted by the upper legform at an impact velocity of 11.1 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.
requirements.test_case: Measure the impactor velocity at impact and confirm 10.9–11.3 m/s.

requirements.text: In case the fascia top extends into the child headform bonnet top test area (WAD 1000 and above), the fascia within the boundaries defined in paragraph 2.16 shall be subject to child headform tests to the front structure.
requirements.test_case: Mark WAD 1000/1700 and the reference lines, and check whether the fascia lies in the child headform test area; if so, include it in the headform tests.

requirements.text: In case the fascia lies within the bonnet top test area, the manufacturer shall identify the zones where the HIC shall not exceed 1,000 (HIC1000 zone) or 1,700 (HIC1700 zone), and the fascia area shall be assigned accordingly.
requirements.test_case: Review the manufacturer's HIC zone drawing and its x/y coordinates covering the fascia area.

requirements.text: In case the fascia lies within the child headform test area, the front structure shall comply with the HIC limit of 1,000 in the HIC1000 zone and 1,700 in the HIC1700 zone at all measuring points, including points near zone borders.
requirements.test_case: Perform child headform impacts on the fascia area, calculate HIC, and compare it with the zone limit.

requirements.text: In case the fascia lies within the child headform test area, the fascia shall be impacted by the child headform at a velocity of 9.7 m/s ± 0.2 m/s at the time of impact.
requirements.test_case: Measure the headform velocity during free flight per ISO 3784 and correct it to the time of impact.

requirements.text: In case the fascia lies within the child headform test area, the fascia shall be impacted in the longitudinal vertical plane at 50° ± 2° to the horizontal, downward and rearward.
requirements.test_case: Verify the launcher angle and the measured velocity vector angle at impact.

requirements.text: In case the fascia lies within the child headform test area, the selected measuring points for the child headform impactor shall be a minimum of 165 mm apart, measured with a flexible tape held tautly along the outer surface of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Measure the spacing between the marked child headform points along the vehicle surface with a taut flexible tape and confirm each pair is at least 165 mm apart.

requirements.text: In case the fascia lies within the child headform test area, the selected child headform measuring points shall lie within the child headform test areas defined in paragraphs 2.16 and 2.44.
requirements.test_case: Mark the child headform bonnet top test area boundaries on the vehicle and confirm all selected points lie inside them.

requirements.text: In case the radar/camera feed an AEBS, the vehicle fitted with the AEBS shall, when activated and operated within the prescribed speed ranges, meet the performance requirements of paragraphs 5.1 and 5.3 to 5.6.
requirements.test_case: Run the tests of paragraph 6 and verify compliance with paragraphs 5.1 and 5.3 to 5.6.

requirements.text: In case the vehicle is submitted to approval for the Car to car scenario, the AEBS shall meet the performance requirements of paragraph 5.2.1.
requirements.test_case: Perform the vehicle target tests of paragraphs 6.4 and 6.5.

requirements.text: In case the vehicle is submitted to approval for the Car to bicycle scenario, the AEBS shall meet the performance requirements of paragraph 5.2.3.
requirements.test_case: Perform the bicycle target tests of paragraph 6.7.

requirements.text: The effectiveness of the AEBS shall not be adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields.
requirements.test_case: Perform EMC immunity tests on the vehicle/ESAs and verify no degradation of the AEBS function.

requirements.text: The immunity of the AEBS shall be demonstrated by fulfilling the technical requirements and respecting the transitional provisions of the 06 series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 10.
requirements.test_case: Test the radar and camera modules/vehicle to UN R10 06 series and check the test reports.

requirements.text: Conformity of the AEBS with the safety aspects of electronic control systems shall be shown by meeting the requirements of Annex 3.
requirements.test_case: Review the Annex 3 documentation and safety concept and perform the Annex 3 verification tests.

requirements.text: In addition to the collision warnings, the AEBS shall provide the driver with the warnings of paragraphs 5.1.4.1 to 5.1.4.3 (failure, non-initialisation information and deactivation warning).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the vehicle and trigger each warning condition to confirm that the warning is present.

requirements.text: The AEBS shall provide a failure warning when there is a failure in the AEBS that prevents the requirements of this Regulation from being met.
requirements.test_case: Induce sensor faults (failure detection test, para 6.8) and verify that the failure warning is given.

requirements.text: The failure warning shall be as specified in paragraph 5.5.4 (constant yellow optical warning signal).
requirements.test_case: Observe the failure warning during the failure detection test.

requirements.text: There shall not be an appreciable time interval between each AEBS self-check.
requirements.test_case: Verify the self-check cycle time by design review and fault injection.

requirements.text: In the case of an electrically detectable failure, there shall not be a delay in illuminating the failure warning signal.
requirements.test_case: Disconnect the sensor power or a sensor connector and measure the time until the warning lights up.

requirements.text: Upon detection of any non-electrical failure condition (e.g. sensor blindness or sensor misalignment), the failure warning signal shall be illuminated.
requirements.test_case: Cover the radar/camera or misalign the sensor bracket and verify that the failure warning lights up.

requirements.text: If the AEBS has not been initialised after a cumulative driving time of 15 seconds above a speed of 10 km/h, information of this status shall be indicated to the driver.
requirements.test_case: Drive with the system prevented from initialising and check that the status indication appears after 15 s above 10 km/h.

requirements.text: The non-initialisation information shall exist until the AEBS has been successfully initialised.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the indication remains until initialisation completes and then clears.

requirements.text: If the vehicle is equipped with a means to deactivate the AEBS, a deactivation warning shall be given when the system is deactivated, as specified in paragraph 5.4.3.
requirements.test_case: Deactivate the AEBS and observe the warning.

requirements.text: Subject to paragraphs 5.3.1 and 5.3.2, the AEBS shall provide emergency braking interventions having the purpose of significantly decreasing the speed of the subject vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Verify the braking interventions during the tests of paragraphs 6.4 to 6.7.

requirements.text: The AEBS shall be designed to minimise the generation of collision warning signals in situations where there is no risk of an imminent collision.
requirements.test_case: Assess the false-reaction scenarios of Annex 3 Appendix 2 and check that no unwarranted warnings occur.

requirements.text: The AEBS shall be designed to avoid advanced emergency braking in situations where there is no risk of an imminent collision.
requirements.test_case: Assess the false-reaction scenarios of Annex 3 Appendix 2 and check that no unwarranted braking occurs.

requirements.text: False reaction avoidance shall be demonstrated in the Annex 3 assessment, which shall include in particular the scenarios listed in Appendix 2 of Annex 3.
requirements.test_case: Review the Annex 3 assessment for coverage of all Appendix 2 scenarios.

requirements.text: Any M1 vehicle fitted with an AEBS shall meet the performance requirements of UN Regulation No. 13-H in its 01 series of amendments.
requirements.test_case: Check the vehicle's UN R13-H 01 series approval.

requirements.text: Any M1 vehicle fitted with an AEBS shall be equipped with an anti-lock braking function in accordance with Annex 6 to UN Regulation No. 13-H in its 01 series of amendments.
requirements.test_case: Check the ABS approval to R13-H Annex 6.

requirements.text: When an imminent collision with a preceding M1 vehicle in the same lane is detected with a relative speed above that up to which the subject vehicle can avoid the collision, a collision warning shall be provided as specified in paragraph 5.5.1.
requirements.test_case: Perform the warning and activation tests with a vehicle target (paras 6.4/6.5) and verify the warning.

requirements.text: The car-to-car collision warning shall be triggered at the latest 0.8 seconds before the start of emergency braking.
requirements.test_case: Measure the time between warning onset and emergency braking onset in the tests of paras 6.4/6.5.

requirements.text: In case the collision cannot be anticipated in time to give a collision warning 0.8 seconds ahead of emergency braking, the collision warning shall be provided no later than the start of the emergency braking intervention.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the warning onset is not later than the braking onset in the test data.

requirements.text: When the system has detected the possibility of an imminent collision with a vehicle target, there shall be a braking demand of at least 5.0 m/s² to the service braking system of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Record the braking demand/deceleration during the tests of paras 6.4/6.5 and check it is at least 5.0 m/s².

requirements.text: The AEBS shall be active, for the car-to-car scenario, at least within the vehicle speed range between 10 km/h and 60 km/h and at all vehicle load conditions, unless deactivated as per paragraph 5.4.
requirements.test_case: Test at speeds across 10-60 km/h at maximum mass and at mass in running order.

requirements.text: In absence of a driver input leading to interruption, the AEBS shall achieve, against a stationary or moving M1 vehicle target, a relative impact speed less than or equal to the maximum relative impact speed of the M1 table, under the stated conditions (flat dry road, ambient illumination of at least 1000 lux, no extreme sensor blinding, target not extreme in RCS/silhouette, no significant weather affecting sensing, lateral offset not more than 0.2 m, straight travel).
requirements.test_case: Perform the vehicle target tests of paras 6.4/6.5 and measure the relative impact speed.

requirements.text: Maximum relative impact speed for M1 (maximum mass / mass in running order): relative speeds 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35 and 40 km/h: 0/0 km/h; 42 km/h: 10/0 km/h; 45 km/h: 15/15 km/h; 50 km/h: 25/25 km/h; 55 km/h: 30/30 km/h; 60 km/h: 35/35 km/h.

source.paragraph: 5.2.1.4. Table Maximum relative Impact Speed for M1 vehicle

requirements.test_case: Compare the measured impact speeds with the table values at each test speed and load.

requirements.text: For relative speeds between the listed values, the maximum relative impact speed assigned to the next higher relative speed shall apply, and for masses above the mass in running order, the value assigned to the maximum mass shall apply.
requirements.test_case: Apply the next higher speed row and the maximum-mass column when evaluating intermediate test points.

requirements.text: When conditions deviate from those listed for the car-to-car scenario, the AEBS shall not deactivate or unreasonably switch the control strategy.
requirements.test_case: Review the Annex 3 demonstration and, if needed, test in deviating conditions.

requirements.text: In case of pedestrian scenario approval, when the AEBS has detected the possibility of a collision with a pedestrian crossing the road at a constant speed of 5 km/h, a collision warning shall be provided as specified in paragraph 5.5.1.
requirements.test_case: Perform the pedestrian target tests of para 6.6 and verify the warning.

requirements.text: In case of pedestrian scenario approval, the pedestrian collision warning shall be provided no later than the start of the emergency braking intervention.
requirements.test_case: Compare the warning onset with the braking onset in the para 6.6 test data.

requirements.text: In case of pedestrian scenario approval, when the system has detected the possibility of an imminent collision, there shall be a braking demand of at least 5.0 m/s² to the service braking system.
requirements.test_case: Record the braking demand in the para 6.6 tests and check it is at least 5.0 m/s².

requirements.text: In case of pedestrian scenario approval, the AEBS shall be active at least within the vehicle speed range between 20 km/h and 60 km/h and at all vehicle load conditions, unless deactivated as per paragraph 5.4.
requirements.test_case: Test at speeds across 20-60 km/h at both load conditions.

requirements.text: In case of pedestrian scenario approval, in absence of a driver input leading to interruption, the AEBS shall achieve an impact speed less than or equal to the maximum impact speed of the M1 table against an unobstructed pedestrian crossing perpendicularly at not more than 5 km/h, under the stated conditions (ambient illumination of at least 2000 lux, no extreme blinding, no significant weather affecting sensing, impact point offset not more than 0.2 m, straight travel, single pedestrian with unambiguous object separation).
requirements.test_case: Perform the para 6.6 tests and measure the impact speed.

requirements.text: Maximum impact speed for M1, pedestrian (maximum mass / mass in running order): subject vehicle speeds 20, 25, 30, 35 and 40 km/h: 0/0 km/h; 42 km/h: 10/0 km/h; 45 km/h: 15/15 km/h; 50 km/h: 25/25 km/h; 55 km/h: 30/30 km/h; 60 km/h: 35/35 km/h.

source.paragraph: 5.2.2.4. Table Maximum Impact Speed for M1 (pedestrian)

requirements.test_case: Compare the measured impact speeds with the table values.

requirements.text: In case of pedestrian scenario approval, for subject vehicle speeds between the listed values, the maximum impact speed assigned to the next higher speed shall apply, and for masses above the mass in running order, the value assigned to the maximum mass shall apply.
requirements.test_case: Apply the interpolation rule when evaluating the test results.

requirements.text: In case of pedestrian scenario approval, when conditions deviate from those listed, the AEBS shall not deactivate or unreasonably switch the control strategy.
requirements.test_case: Review the Annex 3 demonstration and, if needed, test in deviating conditions.

requirements.text: In case of bicycle scenario approval, when the AEBS has detected the possibility of a collision with a bicycle crossing the road at a constant speed of 15 km/h, a collision warning shall be provided as specified in paragraph 5.5.1.
requirements.test_case: Perform the bicycle target tests of para 6.7 and verify the warning.

requirements.text: In case of bicycle scenario approval, the bicycle collision warning shall be provided no later than the start of the emergency braking intervention.
requirements.test_case: Compare the warning onset with the braking onset in the para 6.7 test data.

requirements.text: In case of bicycle scenario approval, when the system has detected the possibility of an imminent collision, there shall be a braking demand of at least 5.0 m/s² to the service braking system.
requirements.test_case: Record the braking demand in the para 6.7 tests and check it is at least 5.0 m/s².

requirements.text: In case of bicycle scenario approval, the AEBS shall be active at least within the vehicle speed range between 20 km/h and 60 km/h and at all vehicle load conditions, unless deactivated as per paragraph 5.4.
requirements.test_case: Test at speeds across 20-60 km/h at both load conditions.

requirements.text: In case of bicycle scenario approval, in absence of a driver input leading to interruption, the AEBS shall achieve an impact speed less than or equal to the maximum impact speed of the M1 table against an unobstructed cyclist crossing perpendicularly at constant speeds between 10 and 15 km/h, under the stated conditions (ambient illumination of at least 2000 lux, no extreme blinding, no significant weather affecting sensing, crankshaft impact point offset not more than 0.2 m, straight travel, single cyclist with unambiguous object separation).
requirements.test_case: Perform the para 6.7 tests and measure the impact speed.

requirements.text: Maximum impact speed for M1, bicycle (maximum mass / mass in running order): subject vehicle speeds 20, 25, 30, 35 and 38 km/h: 0/0 km/h; 40 km/h: 10/0 km/h; 45 km/h: 25/25 km/h; 50 km/h: 30/30 km/h; 55 km/h: 35/35 km/h; 60 km/h: 40/40 km/h.

source.paragraph: 5.2.3.4. Table Maximum Impact Speed for M1 (bicycle)

requirements.test_case: Compare the measured impact speeds with the table values.

requirements.text: In case of bicycle scenario approval, for subject vehicle speeds between the listed values, the maximum impact speed assigned to the next higher speed shall apply, and for masses above the mass in running order, the value assigned to the maximum mass shall apply.
requirements.test_case: Apply the interpolation rule when evaluating the test results.

requirements.text: In case of bicycle scenario approval, when conditions deviate from those listed, the AEBS shall not deactivate or unreasonably switch the control strategy.
requirements.test_case: Review the Annex 3 demonstration and, if needed, test in deviating conditions.

requirements.text: The AEBS shall provide the means for the driver to interrupt the collision warning and the emergency braking.
requirements.test_case: Perform a positive driver action (e.g. kick-down) during an intervention and verify the interruption.

requirements.text: If a means to manually deactivate the AEBS is fitted, the AEBS function shall be automatically reinstated at each initiation of the powertrain (an automatic stop/start restart is not an initiation).
requirements.test_case: Deactivate the AEBS, restart the powertrain and verify that the AEBS is active.

requirements.text: If a means to manually deactivate the AEBS is fitted, manual deactivation shall not be possible with less than two deliberate actions.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the deactivation procedure and count the deliberate actions.

requirements.text: The AEBS control shall be installed so as to comply with UN Regulation No. 121, 01 series of amendments or later.
requirements.test_case: Check the control's identification and location against R121.

requirements.text: It shall not be possible to manually deactivate the AEBS at a speed above 10 km/h.
requirements.test_case: Attempt deactivation above 10 km/h and verify that it is not possible.

requirements.text: If the AEBS is automatically deactivated, the AEBS function shall be automatically reactivated as soon as the conditions that led to the automatic deactivation are no longer present.
requirements.test_case: Create the deactivation condition, remove it and verify reactivation.

requirements.text: Where automatic deactivation of the AEBS results from the driver manually switching off the ESC, this deactivation shall require at least two deliberate actions by the driver.
requirements.test_case: Switch off the ESC and count the actions needed to deactivate the AEBS.

requirements.text: A constant optical warning signal shall inform the driver that the AEBS function has been deactivated.
requirements.test_case: Deactivate the AEBS and verify the constant optical signal.

requirements.text: The collision warning shall be provided by at least two modes selected from acoustic, haptic or optical.
requirements.test_case: Trigger a collision warning and verify that at least two warning modes are present.

requirements.text: The AEBS failure warning shall be a constant yellow optical warning signal.
requirements.test_case: Induce a failure and inspect the colour and steadiness of the signal.

requirements.text: Each AEBS optical warning signal (unless shown in a common space) shall be activated when the ignition switch is turned to the 'on' (run) position or to a manufacturer-designated check position.
requirements.test_case: Switch the ignition on and observe the warning signal check.

requirements.text: The AEBS optical warning signals shall be visible even by daylight.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the visibility of the signals in daylight.

requirements.text: The satisfactory condition of the AEBS optical warning signals must be easily verifiable by the driver from the driver's seat.
requirements.test_case: Check the signals from the driver's seat.

requirements.text: When an optical warning signal indicates that the AEBS is temporarily not available (e.g. due to inclement weather or sensor blockage), the signal shall be constant.
requirements.test_case: Simulate sensor blockage and verify that the availability signal is constant.

requirements.text: At a Periodic Technical Inspection, it shall be possible to confirm the correct operational status of the AEBS by visible observation of the failure warning signal status following a power-ON and any bulb check.
requirements.test_case: Power on the vehicle and verify the failure warning status sequence.

requirements.text: The AEBS (radar/camera sensing integrated in the front bumper) shall meet the performance requirements when tested on a flat, dry, concrete or asphalt road affording good adhesion.
requirements.test_case: Perform the warning and activation tests on a flat, dry, high-adhesion concrete or asphalt track and record the surface condition.

requirements.text: The AEBS shall meet the performance requirements on a test surface with a consistent slope between level and 1 per cent.
requirements.test_case: Survey the track slope (0–1 %) and run the AEBS tests on it.

requirements.text: The AEBS shall meet the performance requirements at ambient temperatures between 0 °C and 45 °C.
requirements.test_case: Record ambient temperature during the test runs and verify AEBS performance at temperatures within 0–45 °C.

requirements.text: The tests shall be performed with a horizontal visibility range that allows the target to be observed throughout the test.
requirements.test_case: Verify and record that visibility allows observation of the target over the full test distance.

requirements.text: The tests shall be performed when there is no wind liable to affect the results.
requirements.test_case: Measure wind speed during the test runs and record it.

requirements.text: Natural ambient illumination shall be homogeneous in the test area and in excess of 1000 lux for the car-to-car scenario, and the AEBS shall meet the car-to-car performance requirements under this illumination.
requirements.test_case: Measure illuminance in the test area with a lux meter (>1000 lux, homogeneous) before the car-to-car runs.

requirements.text: In case the sensing system supports pedestrian targets, natural ambient illumination shall be homogeneous in the test area and in excess of 2000 lux for the car-to-pedestrian scenario.
requirements.test_case: Measure illuminance (>2000 lux, homogeneous) before the car-to-pedestrian runs.

requirements.text: In case the sensing system supports bicycle targets, natural ambient illumination shall be homogeneous in the test area and in excess of 2000 lux for the car-to-bicycle scenario.
requirements.test_case: Measure illuminance (>2000 lux, homogeneous) before the car-to-bicycle runs.

requirements.text: The vehicle with the AEBS shall be tested at the mass in running order with an additional mass of maximum 125 kg including measuring equipment and a possible second person.
requirements.test_case: Weigh the vehicle and run the AEBS tests at mass in running order plus ≤125 kg.

requirements.text: The vehicle with the AEBS shall be tested at the maximum mass, with the load distribution according to the manufacturer's recommendation.
requirements.test_case: Load the vehicle to maximum mass per the manufacturer's distribution and repeat the AEBS tests.

requirements.text: The AEBS shall detect a vehicle target which is a regular high-volume series production M1 passenger car or a soft target representative of a passenger vehicle according to ISO 19206-3:2021, with the target reference point at the most rearward point on its centreline.
requirements.test_case: Conduct car-to-car tests with an ISO 19206-3:2021 soft target or series M1 car and verify detection.

requirements.text: In case the sensing system supports pedestrian targets, the AEBS shall detect a child articulated soft target representative of the human attributes according to ISO 19206-2:2018.
requirements.test_case: Conduct pedestrian tests with an ISO 19206-2:2018 child articulated soft target and verify detection.

requirements.text: In case the sensing system supports bicycle targets, the AEBS shall detect a bicycle soft target representative of a bicycle with adult cyclist according to ISO 19206-4:2020.
requirements.test_case: Conduct bicycle tests with an ISO 19206-4:2020 soft target and verify detection.

requirements.text: In the stationary vehicle target test, the AEBS shall meet the performance requirements when the subject vehicle approaches the stationary target in a straight line for at least two seconds with a centreline offset of not more than 0.2 m and the functional part of the test starts at a distance corresponding to a TTC of at least 4 s.
requirements.test_case: Run the stationary-target test with ≤0.2 m offset and start at TTC ≥4 s, recording warning and braking.

requirements.text: For M1, the stationary vehicle target test shall be conducted at subject vehicle speeds of 20 km/h (+2/-0) at maximum mass and mass in running order, 40 km/h (+0/-2) at maximum mass and 42 km/h (+0/-2) at mass in running order, and 60 km/h (+0/-2) at maximum mass and mass in running order.

source.paragraph: 6.4. Table Subject vehicle test speed for M1 category in stationary target scenario

requirements.test_case: Perform stationary-target runs at each tabulated speed and load condition within tolerance.

requirements.text: In the moving vehicle target test, the AEBS shall meet the performance requirements with the subject vehicle and target travelling in a straight line in the same direction for at least two seconds with a centreline offset of not more than 0.2 m, the target travelling at 20 km/h (+0/-2), and the functional part starting at a TTC of at least 4 s.
requirements.test_case: Run the moving-target test with a 20 km/h target, ≤0.2 m offset and start at TTC ≥4 s.

requirements.text: For M1, the moving vehicle target test shall be conducted at subject vehicle speeds of 30 km/h (+2/-0) and 60 km/h (+0/-2) at both maximum mass and mass in running order.

source.paragraph: 6.5. Table Subject vehicle test speed for M1 category in moving target scenario

requirements.test_case: Perform moving-target runs at 30 and 60 km/h in both load conditions.

requirements.text: In case the sensing system supports pedestrian targets, the AEBS shall meet the performance requirements when the subject vehicle approaches in a straight line for at least two seconds with an impact point centreline offset of not more than 0.1 m, the functional part starting at a TTC of at least 4 s, and the pedestrian target crossing perpendicular at a constant 5 km/h (+0/-0.4) with the impact point on the vehicle longitudinal centreline (tolerance 0.1 m).
requirements.test_case: Run the crossing child-pedestrian test at 5 km/h with centreline impact point and start at TTC ≥4 s.

requirements.text: In case the sensing system supports pedestrian targets, for M1 the pedestrian target test shall be conducted at subject vehicle speeds of 20 km/h (+2/-0) at maximum mass and mass in running order, 40 km/h (+0/-2) at maximum mass and 42 km/h (+0/-2) at mass in running order, and 60 km/h (+0/-2) at maximum mass and mass in running order.

source.paragraph: 6.6.1. Table Subject vehicle test speed for M1 category in pedestrian target scenario

requirements.test_case: Perform pedestrian runs at each tabulated speed and load condition.

requirements.text: In case the sensing system supports pedestrian targets, the AEBS shall meet the performance requirements without any driver control adjustment, other than slight steering corrections to counteract drift, from the start of the functional part until the collision is avoided or the impact point is passed.
requirements.test_case: Monitor driver controls during pedestrian runs and confirm no inputs other than slight steering corrections.

requirements.text: The impact speed with the pedestrian target shall be assessed at the actual contact point between the target and the vehicle, taking into account the vehicle front shape (including the bumper fascia) without additional protective equipment.
requirements.test_case: Determine impact speed from the measured contact point on the unprotected bumper fascia contour.

requirements.text: In case the sensing system supports bicycle targets, the AEBS shall meet the performance requirements when the subject vehicle approaches in a straight line for at least two seconds with a centreline offset to the bicycle crankshaft impact point of not more than 0.1 m, the functional part starting at a TTC of at least 4 s, and the bicycle target crossing perpendicular at a constant 15 km/h (+0/-1), obstructed during its acceleration phase, with the impact point on the vehicle longitudinal centreline (tolerance 0.1 m).
requirements.test_case: Run the crossing bicycle test at 15 km/h with the target obstructed during acceleration and start at TTC ≥4 s.

requirements.text: In case the sensing system supports bicycle targets, for M1 the bicycle target test shall be conducted at subject vehicle speeds of 20 km/h (+2/-0) at maximum mass and mass in running order, 38 km/h (+0/-2) at maximum mass and 40 km/h (+0/-2) at mass in running order, and 60 km/h (+0/-2) at maximum mass and mass in running order.

source.paragraph: 6.7.1. Table Subject vehicle test speed for M1 category in bicycle target scenario

requirements.test_case: Perform bicycle runs at each tabulated speed and load condition.

requirements.text: In case the sensing system supports bicycle targets, the AEBS shall meet the performance requirements without any driver control adjustment, other than slight steering corrections to counteract drift, from the start of the functional part until the collision is avoided or the impact point is passed.
requirements.test_case: Monitor driver controls during bicycle runs and confirm no inputs other than slight steering corrections.

requirements.text: The impact speed with the bicycle target shall be assessed at the actual contact point between the target and the vehicle, taking into account the vehicle front shape (including the bumper fascia).
requirements.test_case: Determine impact speed from the measured contact point on the bumper fascia contour.

requirements.text: When an electrical failure of any AEBS component (e.g. disconnection of the radar or camera module power supply or connection) is simulated, the failure warning signal shall be activated and remain activated not later than 10 s after the vehicle has been driven at a speed greater than 10 km/h.
requirements.test_case: Disconnect power/connector of the radar or camera, drive above 10 km/h and time the failure warning activation (≤10 s).

requirements.text: The failure warning signal shall be reactivated immediately after a subsequent ignition off/on cycle with the vehicle stationary as long as the simulated failure exists.
requirements.test_case: With the failure still simulated, cycle ignition off/on while stationary and verify immediate warning reactivation.

requirements.text: For vehicles equipped with means to manually deactivate the AEBS, the deactivation warning signal shall be activated when the AEBS is deactivated with the ignition on.
requirements.test_case: Deactivate the AEBS with ignition on and verify the warning signal is activated.

requirements.text: For vehicles equipped with means to manually deactivate the AEBS, after an ignition off/on cycle the deactivation warning signal shall not be reactivated, indicating that the AEBS has been reinstated, and this shall be fulfilled without removing the key where the ignition is key-operated.
requirements.test_case: Cycle ignition off/on (without removing the key) and verify the deactivation warning is not shown and AEBS is active.

requirements.text: Each test scenario (one setup, one speed, one load condition, one category) shall be passed by meeting the required performance in two test runs.
requirements.test_case: Perform each scenario twice (one repeat permitted after a failure) and verify two passing runs.

requirements.text: The number of failed test runs within one category shall not exceed 10.0 per cent for Car to Car tests, 10.0 per cent for Car to Pedestrian tests (where approved) and 20.0 per cent for Car to Bicycle tests (where approved).
requirements.test_case: Count failed runs per category over the test campaign and compare with the 10 %/10 %/20 % limits.

requirements.text: A vehicle approved pursuant to this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements of paragraph 5 (AEBS specifications); this includes the production radar/camera modules, bumper fascia and mounting brackets fitted in front of the sensors.
requirements.test_case: Take series-production vehicles with the bumper system fitted and repeat selected paragraph 5 warning and activation tests, then compare the results with the approved type.

requirements.text: In case the radar/camera modules form part of the AEBS ('The System'), The System shall respect, under non-fault and fault conditions, all the appropriate performance requirements specified elsewhere in this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Run the R152 warning and activation tests with the system intact and with injected sensor faults, and check that the performance requirements are met or that a failure warning is given.

requirements.text: The System, including the radar and camera modules, shall be designed to operate in such a way that it does not induce safety critical risks under non-fault and fault conditions.
requirements.test_case: Review the safety concept and hazard analysis, and run fault-injection tests on the sensor modules to confirm no unsafe vehicle reaction occurs.

requirements.text: Each unit of The System (e.g. the radar module and camera module) shall be clearly and unambiguously identifiable, by marking for hardware and by marking or software output for software content, so that hardware and documentation correspond.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module labels and read out the software version via diagnostics, and compare them with the documentation.

requirements.text: Where functions are combined within a single unit or computer but shown in multiple blocks in the block diagram, only a single hardware identification marking shall be used.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module for a single hardware identification marking.

requirements.text: The unit identification shall define the hardware and software version, and the identification shall be changed when a software change alters the function of the unit as far as this Regulation is concerned.
requirements.test_case: Verify the configuration management process and that the software identifier changes after a function-relevant software release.

requirements.text: In case of a failure of The System (e.g. radar or camera failure), the driver shall be warned, for example by a warning signal or message display.
requirements.test_case: Inject radar and camera faults (disconnection, internal fault, blockage) and verify that the driver warning appears.

requirements.text: When The System is not deactivated by the driver (e.g. by ignition off or a dedicated switch), the failure warning shall be present as long as the fault condition persists.
requirements.test_case: Maintain an injected sensor fault and verify the warning persists until the fault is removed or the system is deactivated.

requirements.text: If the chosen provision selects removal of the Higher Level Function, all corresponding output control signals associated with this function shall be inhibited in such a manner as to limit the transition disturbance.
requirements.test_case: Inject a sensor fault while driving and verify that no warning or brake demand outputs are issued and that no abrupt vehicle reaction occurs.

requirements.text: In case the radar/camera sensors feed an AEBS, the system shall implement strategies to minimise the generation of false reactions (collision warning or emergency braking) in the types of scenarios defined in Annex 3 Appendix 2.
requirements.test_case: Review the safety concept and sensor object-classification strategy, then run a sample of the Appendix 2 scenarios on the track to confirm no warning or braking is triggered.

requirements.text: Scenario 1: the system shall avoid a false reaction when the subject vehicle turns left or right at an intersection in front of an oncoming vehicle that is stopped to turn. Guidance parameters: approach at 30 km/h (+0/-2), braking to ≥16 km/h at steering start with TTC ≤2.8 s, then a constant ≥10 km/h through the turn, with TTC ≤1.7 s when the overlap ratio reaches 0 %.
requirements.test_case: Drive the Scenario 1 manoeuvre with the guidance speeds and TTCs and verify that no collision warning or emergency braking occurs.

requirements.text: Scenario 2: the system shall avoid a false reaction when a forward vehicle turns right or left at a corner while the subject vehicle goes straight. Guidance parameters: both vehicles at 40 km/h (+0/-2); the forward vehicle slows to 10 km/h (+0/-2); the subject vehicle is at ≥26 km/h with TTC ≤4.7 s at turn start, then at a constant ≥20 km/h, with TTC ≤2.5 s when the overlap ratio reaches 0 %.
requirements.test_case: Perform the Scenario 2 track manoeuvre with a forward target vehicle and confirm the absence of warning and braking.

requirements.text: Scenario 3: the system shall avoid a false reaction on a small-radius curved road (outer radius ≤25 m) with guard pipes on the outer side and a stationary M1 vehicle placed just outside the guard pipes on the extension of the lane centre. Guidance parameters: approach at 30 km/h (+0/-2), ≥22 km/h at curve entry with TTC ≤1.6 s, then a constant ≥21 km/h, with TTC ≤1.1 s when the overlap ratio reaches 0 %.
requirements.test_case: Drive the curve with guard pipes and a stationary vehicle target per the Scenario 3 guidance and verify no warning or braking.

requirements.text: Scenario 3, in case pedestrian and/or bicycle targets are supported: the system shall avoid a false reaction on the small-radius curved road when a stationary pedestrian or bicycle target is positioned just outside the guard pipes, with TTC ≤1.1 s when the offset ratio to the target centre reaches -100 %.
requirements.test_case: Repeat Scenario 3 with a stationary pedestrian target and a stationary bicycle target and confirm no warning or braking.

requirements.text: Scenario 4: the system shall avoid a false reaction when the subject vehicle changes lane in front of a lane-reduction signboard placed in the centre of the lane. Guidance parameters: constant 40 km/h (+0/-2), TTC to the signboard ≤4.2 s at steering start and ≤3.3 s when the offset ratio to the signboard centre reaches -100 %.
requirements.test_case: Perform the Scenario 4 lane change past a signboard on the track and confirm that no warning or emergency braking is triggered.

requirements.text: While automated driving functions are in longitudinal control of the vehicle (e.g. ALKS is active) and the AEBS function is suspended or its control strategies (braking demand, warning timing) are adapted, the vehicle shall still provide at least the same collision avoidance capabilities as the AEBS function during manual operation.
requirements.test_case: Run the AEBS car-to-car scenarios with the automated longitudinal function active and compare the achieved impact speeds with the manual-operation results.

requirements.text: The AEBS shall have a means to protect against simple unauthorised modification of the operation of the failure warning signal or, alternatively, a secondary means of checking the correct operational status of the AEBS.
requirements.test_case: Review the manufacturer's confidential description of the protection means, or demonstrate the secondary status check (e.g. diagnostic read-out).

requirements.text: In case the AEBS failure warning signal is shown in a common space, it shall be possible to observe that the common space is functional before checking the failure warning signal status at a Periodic Technical Inspection.
requirements.test_case: Power on the vehicle and verify by inspection that the common display space shows a functional check before the AEBS failure warning status is displayed.

requirements.text: The vehicle manufacturer shall identify and manage, for the vehicle type being approved, supplier-related risks, including those arising from the supplied radar and camera modules.
requirements.test_case: Review the cyber security interface agreement and supplier risk records covering the radar and camera modules.

requirements.text: The vehicle manufacturer shall identify the critical elements of the vehicle type and perform an exhaustive risk assessment for the vehicle type, including the radar and camera modules.
requirements.test_case: Audit the vehicle-type TARA for inclusion and criticality classification of the radar and camera modules.

requirements.text: The vehicle manufacturer shall treat/manage the identified risks appropriately.
requirements.test_case: Check that each risk identified for the sensor modules has a documented treatment decision and status.

requirements.text: The risk assessment shall consider the individual elements of the vehicle type and their interactions, including the radar and camera modules and their vehicle network interfaces (CAN/CAN-FD, automotive Ethernet, FlexRay or proprietary point-to-point link, as applicable).
requirements.test_case: Review the TARA for analysis of each sensor-module interface and its data flows to other ECUs.

requirements.text: The risk assessment shall further consider interactions with any external systems, such as spoofing or jamming of the radar and camera sensor inputs from outside the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Review the TARA for external attack paths, e.g. radar spoofing/jamming and camera adversarial or blinding inputs.

requirements.text: While assessing the risks, the vehicle manufacturer shall consider the risks related to all the threats referred to in Annex 5, Part A, as well as any other relevant risk, for the radar and camera modules.
requirements.test_case: Trace each Annex 5 Part A threat to a TARA entry for the sensor modules or to a justified non-applicability.

requirements.text: The vehicle manufacturer shall protect the vehicle type, including the radar and camera modules, against risks identified in the vehicle manufacturer's risk assessment.
requirements.test_case: Verify that each risk identified for the sensor modules is linked to an implemented security control.

requirements.text: Proportionate mitigations shall be implemented in the radar and camera modules to protect the vehicle type.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module security concept and design for the mitigations assigned to each identified risk.

requirements.text: The mitigations implemented shall include all mitigations referred to in Annex 5, Part B and C which are relevant for the risks identified (e.g. secure software update, message authentication, protection or locking of debug ports, protection against physical manipulation).
requirements.test_case: Trace each relevant Annex 5 Part B/C mitigation to its implementation in the module and verify it by test or inspection.

requirements.text: If a mitigation referred to in Annex 5, Part B or C, is not relevant or not sufficient for the risk identified, the vehicle manufacturer shall ensure that another appropriate mitigation is implemented in the radar and camera modules.
requirements.test_case: Review the justification and the alternative control for each non-applied Annex 5 mitigation.

requirements.text: For type approvals first issued before 1 July 2024 and their extensions, if a mitigation measure referred to in Annex 5, Part B or C is technically not feasible for the modules, another appropriate mitigation shall be implemented.
requirements.test_case: Check the technical feasibility assessment and the implemented alternative mitigation.

requirements.text: Prior to type approval, appropriate and sufficient testing shall be performed to verify the effectiveness of the security measures implemented in the radar and camera modules.
requirements.test_case: Perform and review security tests on the modules (penetration testing, fuzzing of network interfaces, debug-port access, secure boot/update tests) against the security requirements.

requirements.text: Measures shall be implemented for the vehicle type, including the radar and camera modules, to detect and prevent cyber-attacks against vehicles of the vehicle type.
requirements.test_case: Inject manipulated or replayed messages and tampered firmware and verify that the module detects and rejects them.

requirements.text: Measures shall be implemented for the vehicle type, including the radar and camera modules, to support the monitoring capability of the vehicle manufacturer with regards to detecting threats, vulnerabilities and cyber-attacks relevant to the vehicle type.
requirements.test_case: Verify that security events in the module (e.g. authentication failures, secure boot failures) are reported or logged for the vehicle monitoring function.

requirements.text: Measures shall be implemented for the vehicle type, including the radar and camera modules, to provide data forensic capability to enable analysis of attempted or successful cyber-attacks.
requirements.test_case: Trigger simulated attacks and verify that security logs are stored and retrievable with sufficient detail and integrity protection.

requirements.text: In case the radar or camera module uses cryptographic modules for cyber security purposes (e.g. SecOC, secure boot), the cryptographic modules shall be in line with consensus standards.
requirements.test_case: Review the algorithms, key lengths and crypto library/HSM against the referenced consensus standards (e.g. NIST, ISO/IEC).

requirements.text: The threats, vulnerabilities and attack methods of Part A and the mitigations of Parts B and C of Annex 5 shall be considered in the risk assessment and in the mitigations implemented for the radar module and the front camera module as part of the vehicle type.
requirements.test_case: Review the risk assessment (TARA) for the radar and camera modules and confirm traceability to each applicable Annex 5 Table A1 entry and its mitigation.
