requirements.text: The threat analysis for the radar and camera modules shall consider possible attack impacts: safe operation of the vehicle affected, vehicle functions stop working, software modified or performance altered, software altered without operational effects, data integrity breach, data confidentiality breach, loss of data availability, and other impacts including criminality.
requirements.test_case: Check that the TARA rates each threat to the radar and camera modules against the listed impact categories.

requirements.text: Where the radar or camera module receives messages or data (e.g. over CAN/CAN-FD, automotive Ethernet, FlexRay or a point-to-point camera link, including diagnostic and proprietary messages), the vehicle shall verify the authenticity and integrity of the messages it receives (M10), to counter spoofing, code injection, untrusted sources, man-in-the-middle/session hijacking, replay and malicious internal, diagnostic or proprietary messages.
requirements.test_case: Inject spoofed, modified and replayed messages on the module interface and verify that they are rejected (e.g. SecOC MAC/freshness check).

requirements.text: The radar and camera module systems shall implement security by design to minimise the risk of code injection through communication channels (M6).
requirements.test_case: Review the security architecture and design documents for the modules for security-by-design measures addressing code injection.

requirements.text: Access control techniques and designs shall be applied to protect the system data and code of the radar and camera modules against manipulation, overwrite, erasure and introduction of data/code through communication channels (M7).
requirements.test_case: Attempt unauthorised write, erase and download services on the module and verify that access is denied without valid authentication.

requirements.text: In case the radar or camera module uses cryptographic protection (secure onboard communication and/or secure boot), security controls shall be implemented for storing the cryptographic keys (e.g. use of Hardware Security Modules) (M11).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the key storage design (HSM/secure element) and attempt key readout through debug and memory interfaces.

requirements.text: In case camera image data or other confidential data is transmitted from the module to or from the vehicle off-board, the confidential data transmitted shall be protected (M12).
requirements.test_case: Capture the off-board transmission and verify encryption and that no plaintext confidential data is present.

requirements.text: Measures to detect and recover from a denial of service attack (e.g. a large number of garbage data sent to the module) shall be employed for the radar and camera modules (M13).
requirements.test_case: Flood the module network interface with garbage frames and verify detection, a safe degraded state and recovery.

requirements.text: Measures to prevent and detect unauthorised access, including an unprivileged user gaining privileged (e.g. root) access, shall be employed for the radar and camera modules (M9).
requirements.test_case: Perform penetration testing for privilege escalation on the module software and verify prevention and detection.

requirements.text: In case the radar or camera module software/firmware can be updated (via wired diagnostic flashing or over the air via the vehicle gateway), secure software update procedures shall be employed (M16), protecting against fabricated, manipulated or invalid update programs or firmware.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to flash unsigned, tampered and downgraded firmware and verify that the module rejects each of them.

requirements.text: In case the radar or camera module supports software updates, security controls shall be implemented for storing the cryptographic keys used to validate updates (M11).
requirements.test_case: Review the storage of update verification keys and verify that the keys are protected against extraction and replacement.

requirements.text: Security controls shall be applied against interference with short range wireless systems or sensors, including manipulation of the 77 GHz radar sensing (M20).
requirements.test_case: Perform radar spoofing/jamming tests and verify that the module detects the interference and responds safely (e.g. plausibility check, degradation warning).

requirements.text: Security controls shall be applied to the external interfaces of the radar and camera modules, including diagnostic access and any debug/test ports, to prevent their use as a point of attack (e.g. code injection or manipulation of parameters) (M22).
requirements.test_case: Test the diagnostic and debug interfaces for authentication (e.g. secure access) and verify that unauthorised access is blocked.

requirements.text: Access control techniques and designs shall be applied to protect the radar and camera module data/code against extraction of proprietary software, unauthorised changes to the electronic ID, circumvention of monitoring, deletion or manipulation of event logs, introduction of malicious software, fabrication of software, and falsification of key function configuration parameters (M7).
requirements.test_case: Attempt firmware readout, ID change, log erasure and parameter modification without authorisation and verify that each attempt fails.

requirements.text: Security controls shall be implemented for storing cryptographic keys in the radar and camera modules (e.g. security modules) to prevent extraction of the keys (M11).
requirements.test_case: Perform hardware and software key extraction attempts (memory dump, side channel) and verify that the keys cannot be recovered.

requirements.text: Measures to detect and recover from a denial of service attack on the internal network (e.g. flooding of the CAN bus or a high rate of messaging provoking ECU faults) shall be employed for the radar and camera modules (M13).
requirements.test_case: Flood the bus at high message rates and verify that the module detects the attack, does not fail unsafely and recovers.

requirements.text: Cybersecurity best practices for software and hardware development shall be followed for the radar and camera modules, addressing insufficient key lengths with long validity, insufficient use of cryptographic algorithms, deprecated cryptographic algorithms, hardware or software failing to stop an attack, and software bugs (M23).
requirements.test_case: Audit the development process and the cryptographic configuration (algorithms, key lengths) against the applicable best practices.

requirements.text: Cybersecurity testing with adequate coverage shall be performed on the radar and camera modules, including verification that development remainders (debug ports, JTAG, development certificates, developer passwords) do not permit access or privilege escalation, and that no superfluous ports are left open.
requirements.test_case: Review the penetration and fuzz test reports and verify that the JTAG/UART ports are disabled or locked and no development credentials remain.

requirements.text: Cybersecurity best practices for system design and system integration shall be followed when integrating the radar and camera modules into the vehicle network, so that network separation cannot be circumvented (M23).
requirements.test_case: Verify by network testing that the module cannot be used to send arbitrary messages into other network segments.

requirements.text: In case image or event data (potentially personal data) is stored in the camera or radar module, best practices for the protection of data integrity and confidentiality shall be followed for storing the personal data (M24).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the stored data for encryption and integrity protection, and verify that it is erased or protected on change of user.

requirements.text: Measures to prevent and detect unauthorised access shall be employed against physical manipulation of the radar and camera modules, such as unauthorised hardware added for man-in-the-middle attacks or replacement of authorised sensors with unauthorised hardware (M9).
requirements.test_case: Replace the module with an unpaired unit or insert a MitM device, and verify that the vehicle detects it (e.g. component authentication) and rejects it.

requirements.text: In case the radar or camera module provides a dedicated environment for the storage and execution of aftermarket software, services, applications or data, appropriate and proportionate measures shall be put in place to secure that dedicated environment.
requirements.test_case: Review the module architecture for aftermarket execution or storage environments and verify the isolation and access-control measures by security testing.

requirements.text: The software of the radar module and the front camera module shall be security assessed, authenticated and integrity protected (M21), so that corrupted applications or software with poor security cannot be used to attack vehicle systems.
requirements.test_case: Review the software security assessment report and verify by test that the modules reject unsigned or modified software images at boot and load time.

requirements.text: In case third-party software is intended or foreseeable to be hosted on the radar or camera module, security controls shall be applied to minimise the risk from that third-party software (M21).
requirements.test_case: Review the third-party software inventory and its security controls, such as isolation and integrity checks, and test that a compromised third-party component cannot reach protected functions.

requirements.text: Measures shall be implemented for defining and controlling user roles and access privileges to the radar and camera modules (e.g. diagnostic, calibration and maintenance access), based on the principle of least access privilege (M18), so that an owner, operator or maintenance engineer cannot be tricked into unintentionally loading malware or enabling an attack.
requirements.test_case: Review the access-role concept and test that each diagnostic or maintenance role can only perform its authorised services, with privileged services rejected without proper authentication.

requirements.text: In case the radar and camera module software is updatable, all initial and updated software versions of the modules, including their integrity validation data, and the relevant hardware components of the type approved system shall be uniquely identifiable.
requirements.test_case: Read the hardware and software part numbers, versions and integrity data (e.g. hash) from each module and check them against the release documentation.

requirements.text: In case the module software is part of a vehicle type with an RXSWIN, the software version(s) present on the radar and camera modules shall be verifiable for consistency with those defined by the relevant RXSWIN.
requirements.test_case: Read the module software versions via the diagnostic interface and compare them with the RXSWIN register.

requirements.text: In case the radar and camera module software is updatable, the authenticity and integrity of software updates shall be protected to reasonably prevent their compromise and reasonably prevent invalid updates.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to flash unsigned, tampered and invalid update packages and verify that the module rejects them.

requirements.text: Where the vehicle type uses an RXSWIN covering the module software, each RXSWIN shall be uniquely identifiable.
requirements.test_case: Review the RXSWIN assignment for the module software and check that it is unique.

requirements.text: When type approval relevant software of the radar or camera module is modified, the RXSWIN shall be updated if the modification leads to a type approval extension or to a new type approval.
requirements.test_case: Audit the change records of the module software and verify that the RXSWIN was updated for each approval-relevant change.

requirements.text: Where an RXSWIN is used, each RXSWIN shall be easily readable in a standardized way via an electronic communication interface, at least by the standard interface (OBD port).
requirements.test_case: Read the RXSWIN through the OBD port with a standard diagnostic tool.

requirements.text: If RXSWINs are not held on the vehicle, the software version(s) of the radar and camera modules relevant to type approvals shall be easily readable in a standardized way via an electronic communication interface, at least by the standard interface (OBD port).
requirements.test_case: Read the module software versions through the OBD port with a standard diagnostic request (e.g. UDS ReadDataByIdentifier).

requirements.text: The RXSWINs and/or software version(s) stored on the radar and camera modules shall be protected against unauthorised modification.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to write the version identifiers without authorization (e.g. without security access) and verify that the write is refused.

requirements.text: In case over-the-air updates are supported, the radar and camera modules shall be able to restore their previous software version after a failed or interrupted update, or be placed into a safe state after such an update.
requirements.test_case: Interrupt an OTA update (power loss, communication loss) and verify that the module rolls back or enters a defined safe state.

requirements.text: In case over-the-air updates are supported, software updates of the modules shall only be executed when the vehicle has enough power to complete the update process, including the power needed for a possible recovery to the previous version or for placing the vehicle into a safe state.
requirements.test_case: Start an OTA update at a low battery state of charge and verify that the update is inhibited.

requirements.text: In case over-the-air updates are supported and the update execution may affect vehicle safety (e.g. AEBS/ACSF functions unavailable), technical means shall ensure that the vehicle is in a state where the update of the radar or camera module can be executed safely.
requirements.test_case: Try to trigger a module update in unsafe vehicle states (e.g. driving) and verify that execution is blocked.

requirements.text: In case over-the-air updates are supported, the defined preconditions shall be met before a software update of the radar or camera module is executed.
requirements.test_case: Violate each defined precondition in turn and verify that the update does not start.

requirements.text: In case an over-the-air update of the radar or camera module requires a skilled action, such as sensor recalibration after programming, the update shall only proceed when a person skilled to do that action is present or is in control of the process.
requirements.test_case: Perform an OTA update that requires recalibration and verify that it cannot complete without an authorized skilled operator step.

requirements.text: In case over-the-air updates of the radar or camera module are supported and executing the update whilst driving may not be safe, the vehicle shall not be able to be driven during the execution of the update.
requirements.test_case: Start an OTA update of the radar/camera module on the vehicle and attempt to drive off; verify that driving is inhibited until the update is completed.

requirements.text: In case over-the-air updates of the radar or camera module are supported and executing the update whilst driving may not be safe, the driver shall not be able to use any vehicle functionality that would affect the safety of the vehicle or the successful execution of the update.
requirements.test_case: During an OTA update of the module, try to operate safety-relevant vehicle functions and verify that they are blocked and that the update completes successfully.

requirements.text: In case the radar and camera modules form part of a DCAS approved under R171, the system shall be designed to guard against unauthorized modification of its software and hardware components, including the radar and camera modules.
requirements.test_case: Review the anti-tampering design (secure boot, signed software, component pairing) of the sensor modules and attempt unauthorized software or hardware replacement.

requirements.text: In case the vehicle is DCAS-equipped, it shall be equipped with an Advanced Emergency Braking System complying with UN R152 (M1) and with a Lane Departure Warning or Lane Departure Prevention System complying with UN R130 or R79 (Corrective Steering Function), as appropriate.
requirements.test_case: Verify that valid R152 and R130/R79 approvals exist for the vehicle using the bumper's radar and camera modules.

requirements.text: In case the radar and camera modules form part of a DCAS, the system shall be able to detect, assess and respond to its surroundings as required to implement the system's intended functionality, within the system boundaries and to the extent possible if operating beyond system boundaries.
requirements.test_case: Run the Annex 4 physical test scenarios and check correct detection of targets and lane markings through the painted fascia within the declared boundaries.

requirements.text: In case the radar and camera modules form part of a DCAS, the system shall aim to detect the applicable system boundaries (e.g. sensor range, visibility, lane marking quality) when DCAS or a DCAS feature is in 'on' mode.
requirements.test_case: Expose the vehicle to declared boundary conditions (degraded markings, reduced visibility, end of range) and verify that the system detects them and changes to 'standby'.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS has a manoeuvre feature (e.g. lane change), the system shall only be permitted to perform a manoeuvre if the vehicle is equipped with detection capabilities with sufficient range to the front, side and rear with respect to the manoeuvre.
requirements.test_case: Measure the forward detection range of the radar and camera installed behind the fascia and compare it with the range needed for the declared manoeuvres.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS is capable of system-initiated manoeuvres or of withholding hands-on requests (hands-off), the system shall have anticipatory behaviour towards other road users, demonstrated by avoiding a collision in the lead-vehicle cut-out, adjacent-vehicle cut-in and decelerating lead vehicle scenarios of Annex 4 (paragraphs 4.2.5.2.6, 4.2.5.2.5 and 4.2.5.2.4), accounting for the robustness criteria of Annex 3 Appendix 4.
requirements.test_case: Perform the Annex 4 cut-out, cut-in and decelerating lead vehicle tests and verify that no collision occurs.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS is capable of system-initiated manoeuvres or of withholding hands-on requests, the system shall, for highway operation, aim to respond to work zones, lane reductions, lane closures, toll stations and end of highways.
requirements.test_case: Drive through work zones, lane closures, toll stations and highway ends and verify that the system notifies the driver, issues a DCA or continues operation as declared.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS is capable of system-initiated manoeuvres or of withholding hands-on requests, the system shall be able to recognize lane markings as outlined in Annex 3 of the 01 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 130, as relevant to the countries in which the system can be activated.
requirements.test_case: Test camera lane marking recognition on the R130 Annex 3 marking types for the target countries.

requirements.text: In case the radar and camera modules form part of a DCAS, the system shall aim to determine the permitted road speed limit relevant to the current lane of travel.
requirements.test_case: Drive past a set of speed limit signs and compare the system-determined speed limit with the posted limit for the lane of travel.

requirements.text: In case the radar and camera modules form part of a DCAS, the activated system shall be capable of detecting and responding to electrical and non-electrical failure conditions (e.g. sensor blockage, misalignment) of the radar and camera modules that affect the safe operation of the system or its features.
requirements.test_case: Inject electrical faults and apply blockage and misalignment to the radar and camera, then verify detection and the failure response.

requirements.text: In case the radar (ACC) and camera (LKA) functions form a DCAS approved under R171: when the driver switches the DCAS to 'off' mode, there shall be no automatic transition to any system that provides continuous longitudinal and/or lateral movement of the vehicle, such as a stand-alone ACC or LKA function.
requirements.test_case: Switch the DCAS off while driving and verify that ACC and LKA do not engage automatically.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS approved under R171: when the DCAS is in 'active' mode, no system other than the DCAS shall provide sustained longitudinal and lateral control assistance, unless an emergency safety system intervention is deemed necessary as specified in paragraph 5.2.
requirements.test_case: With the DCAS active, check function arbitration logs and vehicle behaviour to confirm that no separate ACC or LKA control output is present.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS approved under R171: the DCAS or its features shall only enter 'active' mode if no failure affecting safe operation of the system has been detected, including failures of the radar and camera sensors.
requirements.test_case: Inject a radar or camera fault and attempt activation; verify that the system does not enter 'active' mode.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS approved under R171: the DCAS or its features shall only enter 'active' mode if the system or feature has not detected that it is outside its system boundaries, for example because of sensor blockage, misalignment or missing lane markings.
requirements.test_case: Simulate sensor blockage or absent lane markings and attempt activation; verify that activation is refused.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS approved under R171: when the system or a feature has assessed that the preconditions for remaining in 'active' mode are no longer met (e.g. a sensor failure or a reached system boundary is detected), it shall terminate the control output in a safe and timely manner, either by transitioning to 'stand-by' mode or by switching to 'off' mode.
requirements.test_case: While active, inject a sensor failure or blockage and verify a safe and timely transition to stand-by or off.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS approved under R171: the system shall not resume longitudinal control without driver input if the vehicle comes to a standstill following an intervention by an emergency safety system (e.g. AEBS).
requirements.test_case: Trigger an AEBS stop with the DCAS active and verify that the vehicle does not drive off without driver input.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS approved under R171: a driver brake input producing a higher deceleration than the system-induced deceleration shall override and suspend the longitudinal control assistance during the overriding period.
requirements.test_case: While following a target in active mode, apply the brake harder than the system deceleration and verify that longitudinal assistance is suspended.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS approved under R171: after a brake override, the system shall not resume longitudinal control assistance without a separate driver action, except to avoid inappropriate distances to other road users, or when the driver input reduced the speed by no more than 30 km/h within 2 s.
requirements.test_case: Perform brake overrides with speed reductions above and below 30 km/h within 2 s and verify the resume behaviour.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS approved under R171: after longitudinal control assistance resumes, the rate of increase of acceleration up to the current maximum speed shall be gradual (low jerk) and controllable in accordance with paragraph 5.3.6.
requirements.test_case: Measure longitudinal acceleration and jerk after resumption and verify a gradual increase.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS approved under R171: a driver input to any braking system control (e.g. service brake or parking brake) to hold the vehicle at standstill shall override the longitudinal control assistance.
requirements.test_case: At standstill in active mode, hold the brake or apply the parking brake and verify that the system does not command drive-off.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS approved under R171: a driver accelerator input producing a higher acceleration than the system-induced acceleration shall override the longitudinal control assistance.
requirements.test_case: Press the accelerator beyond the system demand and verify that the driver input takes priority.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS approved under R171: after an accelerator override, the system shall resume longitudinal control assistance on the basis of the current maximum speed.
requirements.test_case: Release the accelerator after an override and verify that the set speed resumes as the current maximum speed.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS approved under R171: a driver steering input shall override any feature of the lateral control assistance.
requirements.test_case: Apply a steering input during lane keeping and verify that the lateral assistance is overridden.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS approved under R171: the steering control effort needed to override the lateral control assistance shall not exceed 50 N.
requirements.test_case: Measure the steering-wheel rim force at the moment of override and verify that it is at most 50 N.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS approved under R171: the system shall inform or warn the driver if, while in 'active' mode, it has detected that it has reached a currently relevant system boundary, unless this is already indicated by the system status.
requirements.test_case: Drive into a boundary condition (e.g. lane markings end) and verify the driver information.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS approved under R171: the system shall inform or warn the driver about a detected upcoming system boundary.
requirements.test_case: Approach a detectable upcoming boundary and verify that a timely warning is given.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS approved under R171: the system shall inform or warn the driver about detected failures affecting the system or its features, including radar or camera failures, unless the system is in 'off' mode.
requirements.test_case: Inject a radar or camera fault in stand-by and in active mode and verify the failure information to the driver.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS is hands-off capable (HORs withheld): an HOR required by a detected upcoming boundary condition shall be given at the latest 5 seconds before the boundary condition is reached.
requirements.test_case: In hands-off mode, approach a boundary (e.g. end of lane markings) and measure the time from the HOR to reaching the boundary.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS is hands-off capable (HORs withheld): for boundary situations not detected 5 seconds in advance, a DCA shall be issued, unless lateral assistance will still be provided after the driver is motorically re-engaged.
requirements.test_case: Present a boundary that is detectable only late in hands-off mode and verify that a DCA is issued.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS is hands-off capable (HORs withheld): where a DCA is not issued for a late-detected boundary, an HOR shall be issued upon detection of the upcoming boundary condition(s).
requirements.test_case: Present a boundary that is detectable only late while lateral assistance continues and verify that an HOR is issued immediately on detection.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS approved under R171 providing positioning in the lane of travel on an M1 vehicle, the feature may induce lateral acceleration higher than 3 m/s² only while all of these conditions are met: (a) the system gives the driver visual information on the upcoming or ongoing situation that may induce such acceleration; (b) no disengagement warning is being given; (c) operation remains predictable and controllable per para. 5.3.6; (d) the vehicle travels at or below the system-determined road speed limit; and (e) the driver is not determined to be motorically disengaged.
requirements.test_case: Drive curves inducing more than 3 m/s² lateral acceleration and record that such acceleration occurs only with visual information shown and all conditions (a) to (e) met.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS providing positioning in the lane of travel with increased lateral dynamics, when any of the conditions of para. 6.1.1.1 (a) to (e) is no longer met, the system shall implement strategies to ensure controllability.
requirements.test_case: Invalidate one condition at a time (e.g. exceed the speed limit, trigger driver disengagement) during a high-lateral-acceleration curve and verify the controllability strategy is applied.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS can assist on merging roads, the system shall aim to detect situations where the current lane of travel merges into another lane, including slip roads.
requirements.test_case: Drive merge and slip-road scenarios and log the system's merge detection.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS can assist on merging roads, the system shall be designed to ensure safe control in merging situations, accounting for road users in the neighbouring lane.
requirements.test_case: Run merge scenarios with target vehicles in the neighbouring lane and verify safe gap keeping without conflict.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS can form an access corridor for emergency and enforcement vehicles, the system shall leave its current lane of travel to (pre-emptively) form the corridor only where national traffic rules require and allow this.
requirements.test_case: Test corridor scenarios in traffic jams and non-jam conditions and verify the corridor is formed only where required and allowed.

requirements.text: While forming an access corridor, the system shall ensure sufficient lateral and longitudinal distance to road boundaries, vehicles and other road users.
requirements.test_case: Measure lateral and longitudinal distances to boundaries and targets during corridor formation.

requirements.text: The vehicle shall return completely to its original lane of travel once the situation that required the access corridor has passed.
requirements.test_case: After the corridor situation ends, verify the vehicle returns fully to its original lane.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS performs lane positioning on roads without lane markings, the system shall use other sources of information to robustly determine and pursue the appropriate trajectory with respect to other road users.
requirements.test_case: Drive unmarked roads with and without other road users and verify a robust, appropriate trajectory.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS assists lane changes, a lane change shall only be performed if the system has sufficient information about its surroundings to the front, side and rear to assess the criticality of the lane change.
requirements.test_case: Degrade or block sensor coverage and verify lane changes are suppressed.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS assists lane changes, a lane change shall not be performed towards a lane intended for traffic moving in the opposite direction.
requirements.test_case: Request lane changes towards an oncoming-traffic lane and verify none is performed.

requirements.text: During a DCAS lane change manoeuvre, the system shall be designed to avoid a lateral acceleration of more than 1.5 m/s² in addition to the lateral acceleration generated by the lane curvature.
requirements.test_case: Measure lateral acceleration during lane changes on straight and curved roads.

requirements.text: During a DCAS lane change manoeuvre, the system shall be designed to avoid a total lateral acceleration in excess of 3.5 m/s².
requirements.test_case: Measure total lateral acceleration during lane changes in curves.

requirements.text: During a DCAS lane change, the moving average over half a second of the lateral jerk generated by the system shall not exceed 5 m/s³.
requirements.test_case: Compute the 0.5 s moving average of lateral jerk from logged data during lane changes.

requirements.text: A DCAS lane change manoeuvre shall only be started if a vehicle in the target lane is not forced to decelerate unmanageably because of the lane change.
requirements.test_case: Run lane changes with approaching vehicles in the target lane and verify their required deceleration stays manageable.

requirements.text: When there is an approaching vehicle, the system shall be designed not to make it decelerate at more than 3.0 m/s², so that the distance between the two vehicles is never less than the distance the DCAS vehicle travels in 1 second.
requirements.test_case: Run approaching-vehicle lane-change tests and evaluate the required deceleration and minimum gap.

requirements.text: The approaching-vehicle assessment shall assume the approaching vehicle begins decelerating 1.4 s after the system starts the lateral movement, and either 0.4 s after the lane change manoeuvre starts (only if the vehicle was detected for at least 1.0 s immediately before the manoeuvre started) or 1.4 s after the manoeuvre starts.
requirements.test_case: Check the lane-change decision logic against the prescribed reaction-time assumptions in the test evaluation.

requirements.text: If no approaching vehicle is detected in the target lane, the assessment shall assume an approaching vehicle (a) at a distance equal to the actual rearward detection range, (b) travelling at the allowed maximum speed or 130 km/h, whichever is lower, and (c) with its full width detected for at least 1 s during its lateral movement; on a just-commenced target lane the requirement is deemed fulfilled if no vehicle is detected along the target lane to the rear.
requirements.test_case: Verify lane-change initiation logic against the actual detection range and the assumed approaching speed.

requirements.text: In case the system intends to decelerate the vehicle during a lane change procedure, this deceleration shall be factored in when assessing the distance to a vehicle approaching from the rear.
requirements.test_case: Test lane changes with planned deceleration and verify the rear gap assessment includes it.

requirements.text: The system's deceleration during a lane change procedure shall not exceed 2 m/s², except to avoid or mitigate the risk of an imminent collision.
requirements.test_case: Measure longitudinal deceleration during lane change procedures.

requirements.text: Where the vehicle behind has insufficient headway time at the end of the lane change procedure, the system shall not increase the rate of deceleration for at least 2 s after completing the lane change, except where needed for nominal operation (e.g. responding to infrastructure or road users) or to avoid or mitigate an imminent collision.
requirements.test_case: Complete a lane change with a close following vehicle and check that deceleration does not increase within 2 s.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS assists lane changes, the system shall generate a signal to activate the direction indicator unless the driver has already activated it.
requirements.test_case: Observe direction indicator activation at the start of system-assisted lane changes.

requirements.text: The direction indicator signal shall remain active throughout the whole lane change procedure.
requirements.test_case: Log the indicator status over the full lane change procedure.

requirements.text: The direction indicator signal shall be deactivated by the system in a timely manner once the positioning in the lane of travel feature resumes, unless the direction indicator control remains fully engaged (latched).
requirements.test_case: Check the indicator deactivation time after the lane change completes.

requirements.text: A lane change procedure shall be indicated to other road users for at least 3 seconds before the lane change manoeuvre starts; a shorter time is permitted only where national traffic rules allow it and sufficient notice is still given.
requirements.test_case: Measure the time from indicator activation to start of lateral movement.

requirements.text: When the system suppresses a lane change procedure, it shall clearly inform the driver by an optical signal combined with an acoustic or haptic signal.
requirements.test_case: Create a suppression condition and verify the optical plus acoustic or haptic information is given.

requirements.text: For driver-confirmed lane changes, the system shall aim not to make an approaching vehicle in the target lane decelerate unreasonably, particularly when the lane change is not urgent.
requirements.test_case: Run non-urgent overtaking lane changes with approaching vehicles and evaluate their induced deceleration.

requirements.text: For driver-confirmed lane changes where making a target-lane vehicle decelerate is necessary due to the traffic situation, the requirements of para. 6.2.4.1 shall apply.
requirements.test_case: Run lane-ending and dense-traffic scenarios and check compliance with the 3.0 m/s² and 1 s distance criteria.

requirements.text: For driver-confirmed lane changes, a lane change procedure shall only be proposed if sufficient free space in the target lane is available, or can reasonably be expected to become available, to execute the manoeuvre per para. 6.2.4.
requirements.test_case: Verify that no lane change is proposed when the target lane is occupied without an expected gap.

requirements.text: For driver-confirmed lane changes with no detected approaching vehicle, the assumed approaching vehicle speed shall be the allowed maximum speed + 10 % or 130 km/h, whichever is lower.
requirements.test_case: Check the lane-change assessment logic uses the +10 % speed assumption.

requirements.text: For system-initiated lane changes, the system shall aim to detect restricted lanes (e.g. bus, bike or taxi lanes).
requirements.test_case: Drive past marked bus, bike and taxi lanes and log restricted-lane detection.

requirements.text: For system-initiated lane changes, the system shall aim to refrain from initiating lane changes into restricted lanes.
requirements.test_case: Verify no system-initiated lane change is made into a restricted lane.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS assists lane changes on roads without physical separation of opposing traffic, the system shall implement strategies to ensure the lane change is only performed into or via a lane that is not designated for oncoming traffic.
requirements.test_case: Run the corresponding Annex 4 tests on undivided roads and verify no lane change into an oncoming lane.

requirements.text: The system shall only perform a lane change on roads where pedestrians and cyclists are not prohibited if it is able to avoid causing a risk of collision with any vulnerable road user.
requirements.test_case: Run lane change scenarios with pedestrian and cyclist targets and verify no collision risk is created.

requirements.text: The time between initiation of the lane change procedure and start of the lane change manoeuvre shall not exceed 7 seconds, unless extending it does not violate national traffic rules.
requirements.test_case: Measure the time from lane change procedure initiation to start of the manoeuvre.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS performs manoeuvres other than a lane change, the system shall be designed to respond to vehicles, road users, infrastructure or a blocked path ahead that are within, or may enter, the planned trajectory or its driving environment, to ensure safe operation.
requirements.test_case: Run Annex 4 manoeuvre scenarios with targets entering the planned path and verify a safe response.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS performs other manoeuvres, the system shall be designed to respond, where relevant to the manoeuvre and operating domain, to traffic lights, stop signs, right-of-way infrastructure (e.g. zebra crossings, bus stops) and restricted lanes for its current lane of travel or the lane resulting from the manoeuvre.
requirements.test_case: Run manoeuvres approaching traffic lights, stop signs and zebra crossings and verify correct responses.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS performs other manoeuvres, the system shall be designed to safely and cautiously navigate hillcrests where relevant to the controllability of the manoeuvre.
requirements.test_case: Perform manoeuvres over hillcrests and evaluate speed adaptation and behaviour.

requirements.text: If a manoeuvre could lead the system to cross paths with vulnerable road users crossing the lane of travel (e.g. bike path, crosswalk), the system shall be designed to respond appropriately to these road users and the infrastructure.
requirements.test_case: Run turning manoeuvres with pedestrian and cyclist targets on crosswalks and bike paths and verify an appropriate response.

requirements.text: If a manoeuvre would lead the system to cross paths with crossing traffic or merge with traffic from a different direction, the system shall be designed to respond appropriately to these road users (e.g. by giving way).
requirements.test_case: Run intersection turns with crossing target vehicles and verify the system gives way.

requirements.text: Where relevant to the manoeuvre, the system shall be designed to detect restricted lanes of travel (e.g. bus, bike or taxi lanes).
requirements.test_case: Drive manoeuvres near restricted lanes and log their detection.

requirements.text: Where relevant to the manoeuvre, the system shall aim to refrain from navigating on restricted lanes of travel.
requirements.test_case: Verify manoeuvre paths avoid restricted lanes.

requirements.text: If the system detects that it has entered a restricted lane of travel, it shall propose or perform a lane change to an appropriate lane, as suits the system design, or request the driver to resume manual control.
requirements.test_case: Place the vehicle in a restricted lane and verify a lane change proposal or a driver takeover request.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS performs other manoeuvres, the system shall aim to respect appropriate right-of-way rules.
requirements.test_case: Evaluate right-of-way behaviour in intersection and roundabout scenarios.

requirements.text: Navigating around an obstruction in the lane of travel shall only be permitted if the system can determine the position and movement of other road users to the front, side and rear, where relevant to the manoeuvre, and that there is adequate distance to them.
requirements.test_case: Run obstruction-bypass scenarios with surrounding targets and verify the manoeuvre occurs only with adequate distance.

requirements.text: If navigating around an obstruction would cause the vehicle to cross partially or fully into another lane, the system shall only do so if it can confirm that sufficient space and time are available, with no oncoming road users impeding its return to the appropriate lane.
requirements.test_case: Run bypass scenarios with oncoming targets at varying distances and verify the manoeuvre is aborted or withheld when space is insufficient.

requirements.text: The system shall not cross into a lane with the opposite direction of travel to pass general traffic moving at an appropriate speed.
requirements.test_case: Follow normally moving traffic on an undivided road and verify no passing into the oncoming lane.

requirements.text: The system shall appropriately indicate the manoeuvre around an obstruction to other road users throughout the manoeuvre.
requirements.test_case: Check direction indicator activation throughout the bypass manoeuvre.

requirements.text: The system shall not suggest to the driver, or perform as system-initiated, a manoeuvre that crosses a solid lane marking not permitted to be crossed, unless permitted by legitimate external instruction per para. 6.3.9.1 (c).
requirements.test_case: Present obstructions next to solid lane markings and verify no crossing is suggested or performed without external instruction.

requirements.text: In case the radar and camera modules are part of a DCAS approved under UN R171, the system shall respect, under non-fault and fault conditions, all the appropriate performance requirements specified elsewhere in UN R171.
requirements.test_case: Review the safety analysis and run the R171 performance tests with and without injected sensor faults.

requirements.text: In case the radar and camera modules are part of a DCAS approved under UN R171, the system shall be designed to operate in such a way that it is free of unreasonable safety risks to the driver, passengers and other road users.
requirements.test_case: Assess the hazard/risk analysis covering sensor-originated hazards for completeness and residual risk.

requirements.text: Each unit of the system (radar module, camera module) shall be clearly and unambiguously identifiable, by marking for hardware and by marking or software output for software content, to give the link between hardware and documentation.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module labels and read out the software identification via diagnostics, then compare both with the documentation.

requirements.text: Where functions are combined within a single unit but shown in several blocks in the block diagram, only a single hardware identification marking shall be used for that unit.
requirements.test_case: Inspect that each physical module carries only one hardware identification.

requirements.text: The unit identification shall define the hardware and software version, and the identification shall be changed where a software change alters the function of the unit as far as UN R171 is concerned.
requirements.test_case: Audit the change-management records to confirm that function-altering software releases received a new identification.

requirements.text: The strategy chosen to achieve the system objectives shall not, under non-fault conditions, prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle, supported by an explanation and a validation plan.
requirements.test_case: Review the strategy explanation and the completed validation plan results.

requirements.text: The system shall incorporate design provisions that generate safe operation under fault conditions (e.g. fall-back to a partial system, change-over to a back-up system, or removal of the high-level function).
requirements.test_case: Inject radar and camera faults (signal loss, blockage, misalignment) and observe the system's fault reaction.

requirements.text: If the chosen fault provision is removal of the higher-level function, all output control signals associated with this function shall be inhibited in a manner that limits the transition disturbance.
requirements.test_case: Inject a sensor fault during active assistance and measure that control outputs are inhibited without abrupt vehicle motion.

requirements.text: Measures shall be in place to ensure the system does not prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle when its performance is affected by environmental conditions, e.g. climatic conditions, temperature, dust ingress, water ingress or ice packing.
requirements.test_case: Test the sensors with dirt, water, snow and ice layers on the fascia or lens and at temperature extremes, and verify safe degradation or a blockage warning.

requirements.text: When the system is tested under non-fault conditions, the verification results shall correspond with the description of the functions, including the control strategies, provided by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Run the selected function tests and compare the observed behaviour with the declared description.

requirements.text: When failures in individual units are simulated, the verification results shall correspond with the documented summary of the failure analysis, so that the safety concept and its execution are confirmed as adequate.
requirements.test_case: Simulate internal faults of the radar and camera outputs and compare the system reaction with the failure analysis.

requirements.text: The system behaviour shall be adequate from a controllability perspective under both non-fault and fault conditions.
requirements.test_case: Assess driver controllability in vehicle tests with sensor faults and at sensor boundaries.

requirements.text: In case the radar and camera modules form part of a DCAS approved under R171 (combined sustained lateral and longitudinal control), the detection capabilities of the DCAS shall be explained, differentiated by DCAS feature where applicable (e.g. positioning in the lane, lane change, other manoeuvres), together with the system boundaries of these detection capabilities.
requirements.test_case: Review the detection-capability and system-boundary declaration for each DCAS feature against radar and camera sensor test data, including radar transmission through the painted fascia and the camera field of view.

requirements.text: In case the radar and camera modules are part of a DCAS approved under R171, the system shall be considered to possess a declared capability only if it demonstrates the required behaviour in at least 90% of the corresponding Annex 4 tests.
requirements.test_case: Run the Annex 4 base tests for each declared capability and check that the required behaviour is achieved in at least 90% of the runs.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS approved under R171, when conditions deviate from those specified for the corresponding test, the system shall not unreasonably switch its control strategy.
requirements.test_case: Repeat selected Annex 4 scenarios with varied parameters (speed, offset, target type) and check that the control strategy stays consistent.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS with sustained longitudinal control, the system shall avoid a collision without driver intervention in each declared response-to-other-road-users scenario up to the maximum operational speed declared by the manufacturer, with a deceleration demand not exceeding 5 m/s² or exceeding 5 m/s², as declared. Scenarios, as relevant to system design: stationary vehicle ahead on straight road (4.2.5.2.1.1, highway); stationary vehicle ahead on curved road (4.2.5.2.2.1, highway); slower moving vehicle ahead on straight road (4.2.5.2.3.1, highway); decelerating lead vehicle up to 4 m/s² (4.2.5.2.4.1, highway and non-highway); cut-out of lead vehicle (4.2.5.2.5.1, highway); cut-in vehicle from adjacent lane Type 1 and Type 2 (4.2.5.2.6.1, highway); stationary pedestrian ahead (4.2.5.2.7.1, non-highway); stationary bicycle ahead (4.2.5.2.8.1, non-highway); pedestrian crossing into path (4.2.5.2.9.1, non-highway); bicycle crossing into path (4.2.5.2.10.1, non-highway).
requirements.test_case: Perform each listed Annex 4 scenario up to the declared maximum speed and verify collision avoidance and the deceleration level used.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS with positioning in the lane of travel, the system shall follow the course of the lane within the speed range(s) and between the minimum and maximum lateral acceleration declared by the manufacturer, under the declared specific conditions.

source.paragraph: Annex 3 Appendix 4 2. Table Annex 3 Appendix 4 para 2

requirements.test_case: Drive lane-keeping tests across the declared speed ranges and curve radii and verify lane following up to the declared lateral acceleration.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS, the system shall respond to each road attribute as declared by the manufacturer: treat it as a system boundary, respond upon detection, or provide an early warning. The road attributes are toll station, end of highway, permanent lane ending, temporary lane ending, long-term construction zone, railway crossings, intersections, roundabouts, pedestrian crossing, stop sign, give-way sign and traffic lights.

source.paragraph: Annex 3 Appendix 4 2.1. Table Annex 3 Appendix 4 para 2.1

requirements.test_case: Approach each declared road attribute in testing and verify that the system responds or warns as declared, or treats it as a system boundary.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS is equipped with a lane change feature, the maximum response range shall be reduced only under the conditions declared by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Verify the detection range under nominal and declared degraded conditions against the declarations.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS performs other driver- or system-initiated manoeuvres or responds to targets in non-highway environments, the system shall avoid a collision under the declared preconditions in each scenario declared as handled: pedestrian crossing into the path of the VUT in an intersection (4.2.5.2.11.1), bicycle crossing into the path of the VUT in an intersection (4.2.5.2.12.1), VUT turning across the path of an oncoming vehicle (4.2.5.2.13.1), VUT crossing the straight path of a vehicle target in an intersection (4.2.5.2.14.1), and system-initiated manoeuvring around an obstruction in the lane (4.2.5.2.15).

source.paragraph: Annex 3 Appendix 4 4. Table Annex 3 Appendix 4 para 4

requirements.test_case: Run the declared Annex 4 intersection and obstruction scenarios under the declared preconditions and verify collision avoidance.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS with driver-initiated manoeuvres such as lane change, the system shall obey the traffic rules declared by the manufacturer for that manoeuvre (e.g. duration of indication of the lane change procedure), including any country-specific behaviour declared.

source.paragraph: Annex 3 Appendix 4 5. Table Annex 3 Appendix 4 para 5

requirements.test_case: Perform driver-initiated lane changes and measure the indication duration and other declared rule behaviours against the declaration.

requirements.text: In case the radar and camera modules are part of a DCAS approved under UN R171: when conditions deviate from those specified for the base test, the system shall not unreasonably switch its control strategy (verified by extended testing with each parameter varied).
requirements.test_case: Run the extended track tests with varied target type, offset, speed and curvature, and compare the control strategy with the base test.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS: for conditions not tested that may occur within the declared system boundaries, the vehicle shall be shown to be safely controlled, as part of the Annex 3 audit.
requirements.test_case: Audit the manufacturer's evidence (simulation and test data) for safe control in untested conditions within the system boundaries.

requirements.text: In case the camera supports positioning in the lane of travel: the system shall achieve the positioning in the lane of travel capability declared by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Base track test on a curved, marked lane comparing the measured lane position with the declared capability.

requirements.text: In case of positioning in the lane of travel: the system shall keep the vehicle positioned in the lane with no driver force on the steering control, at constant speed on a curved track with lane markings on each side, where the lateral acceleration needed to follow the curve is 80–90 % of the declared maximum lateral acceleration, for each declared speed range.
requirements.test_case: Hands-off constant-speed curve test at 80–90 % of the declared maximum lateral acceleration for each speed range, measuring lateral position.

requirements.text: In case of positioning in the lane of travel: the system shall meet the applicable requirements of paragraphs 5.3.7.1 and 6.1 when driven hands-off through a curve whose speed and radius provoke a lateral acceleration higher than the declared maximum lateral acceleration plus 0.3 m/s².
requirements.test_case: Drive hands-off through a curve demanding more than the declared maximum plus 0.3 m/s² and assess the system response against paras. 5.3.7.1 and 6.1.

requirements.text: In case of positioning in the lane of travel: the system shall not leave its lane.
requirements.test_case: Extended track tests at different curvatures (including the S-bend of para. 4.2.4.1) and speeds, monitoring lane departure.

requirements.text: In case of positioning in the lane of travel: the system shall maintain a stable motion inside its ego lane across the speed range and the different curvatures within its system boundaries, up to the declared maximum lateral acceleration.
requirements.test_case: Extended track tests across the speed range and curvatures, evaluating lateral position stability.

requirements.text: In case of positioning in the lane of travel: the lane positioning behaviour shall be maintained with the different types of lane boundaries applicable to the system (e.g. markings, road edges, only one lane marking).
requirements.test_case: Track tests with marked lanes, road edges and single-marking lanes, checking lane positioning.

requirements.text: In case of driver-initiated lane change assistance: after the driver has initiated the lane change procedure, the vehicle shall perform a full lane change (e.g. 3.5 m lateral displacement) into the adjacent lane.
requirements.test_case: Base track test: driver initiates the lane change procedure and the lateral displacement into the adjacent lane is measured.

requirements.text: In case of driver-initiated lane change assistance: the system shall assist the driver in changing lanes safely within its declared boundaries, including on roads without physical separation, on roads where pedestrians and cyclists are not prohibited, where the lane change cannot be executed immediately after initiation, and with a lead vehicle present.
requirements.test_case: Extended track tests with oncoming or overtaking traffic, road users approaching from the rear, a vehicle beside the VUT and a vehicle cutting into the target space.

requirements.text: In case of driver-confirmed or system-initiated lane changes: after the system has initiated the lane change procedure, the vehicle shall perform a full lane change (e.g. 3.5 m lateral displacement) into the adjacent lane.
requirements.test_case: Base track test behind a lead vehicle, measuring the completed lateral displacement into the adjacent lane.

requirements.text: In case of driver-confirmed or system-initiated lane changes: the system shall assist the driver in changing lanes safely, including with other speed differences to the lead vehicle, on roads without physical separation and on roads where pedestrians and cyclists are not prohibited.
requirements.test_case: Extended track tests with traffic in the target lane, rear-approaching and adjacent vehicles, and cut-in conflicts.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS: the system shall achieve its declared response capability to a stationary vehicle ahead on a straight section of road.
requirements.test_case: Straight-road approach to a stationary vehicle target (offset ≤ 0.5 m), comparing the response with the Annex 3 Appendix 4 declaration.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS: the system shall achieve its declared response capability to a stationary vehicle ahead on a curved section of road (target in the first turn of the para. 4.2.4.1 geometry, rear corner touching the extrapolated lane line).
requirements.test_case: Curve test with a stationary target placed at the start of the bend, comparing the response with the declaration.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS: the system shall achieve its declared response capability to a slower moving vehicle ahead on a straight road travelling 50 km/h slower than the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Straight-road test with a target 50 km/h slower than the VUT, comparing the response with the declaration.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS: while following a lead vehicle at 50 km/h at a steady-state time gap maintained by the system, the system shall achieve its declared response capability to the lead vehicle decelerating at up to 4 m/s².
requirements.test_case: Following test at 50 km/h with the target braking at up to 4 m/s², evaluating the VUT response.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS: the system shall achieve its declared response capability when a lead M1 vehicle cuts out to reveal a stationary vehicle target.
requirements.test_case: Cut-out test per the table in para. 4.2.5.2.5.1.3, comparing the response with the declaration.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS: cut-out base test parameters: cut-out at TTC = 3 s; VUT 70 km/h; lead M1 vehicle 50 km/h; lane change lateral acceleration 1.5 m/s²; lane change length 44 m; radius of turning segment 130 m.
requirements.test_case: Perform the cut-out test with the tabulated speeds and manoeuvre parameters.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS: the system shall achieve its declared response capability to a vehicle cutting in from the adjacent lane.
requirements.test_case: Cut-in tests per the table in para. 4.2.5.2.6.1.3, comparing the response with the declaration.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS: cut-in base test parameters: Type 1 – cut-in at TTC = 0 s, VUT 50 km/h, target 10 km/h, lateral acceleration 0.5 m/s², lane change length 14 m, turning radius 15 m; Type 2 – cut-in at TTC = 1.5 s, VUT 120 km/h, target 70 km/h, lateral acceleration 1.5 m/s², lane change length 60 m, turning radius 250 m.
requirements.test_case: Perform Type 1 and Type 2 cut-in tests with the tabulated parameters.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS: the system shall achieve its declared response capability to a stationary pedestrian in the driving path facing away from the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Straight approach to an ISO 19206-2 pedestrian target in the path, comparing the response with the declaration.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS: the system shall achieve its declared response capability to a stationary bicycle in the driving path, including any lateral movement navigating around the target, if applicable.
requirements.test_case: Straight approach to an ISO 19206-4 bicycle target in the path, comparing the response with the declaration.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS: the system shall achieve its declared response capability to a pedestrian crossing perpendicular into the vehicle path at 5 km/h, with a nominal impact point on the vehicle centreline.
requirements.test_case: Crossing pedestrian test at 5 km/h starting from TTC ≥ 4 s, evaluating the response.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS: the system shall achieve its declared response capability to a bicycle crossing perpendicular into the vehicle path at 15 km/h, obstructed during its acceleration phase.
requirements.test_case: Crossing bicycle test at 15 km/h with an obstructed acceleration phase, evaluating the response.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS operates in non-highway intersections: the system shall achieve its declared response capability to a pedestrian crossing into the vehicle path in an intersection.
requirements.test_case: Intersection test with a pedestrian target at 5 km/h on the near side, evaluating the response.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS operates in non-highway intersections: the response to crossing pedestrians in an intersection shall be maintained under variation of the visibility conditions (e.g. night time), as appropriate to the declared system boundaries.
requirements.test_case: Repeat the intersection pedestrian test at night and compare the response.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS operates in non-highway intersections: the system shall achieve its declared response capability to a bicycle crossing into the vehicle path in an intersection at 15 km/h.
requirements.test_case: Intersection crossing bicycle test at 15 km/h, evaluating the response.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS supports turning in intersections: the system shall achieve its declared response capability to an oncoming vehicle (passenger car or motorcycle approaching at up to 60 km/h) while the vehicle turns across its path.
requirements.test_case: Turn-across-path test with 50 % overlap and a target at up to 60 km/h, evaluating the response.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS operates in intersections: the vehicle shall give right of way to a crossing vehicle target (passenger car or motorcycle) approaching straight at up to 60 km/h.
requirements.test_case: Intersection crossing test with the target at up to 60 km/h, checking that the VUT yields.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS supports system-initiated manoeuvres around an obstruction: the vehicle shall avoid collision with the static target and with the vehicle approaching from the opposite direction in the adjacent lane (both vehicles at least 30 km/h, static target at 50 % overlap).
requirements.test_case: Track test with a static target and a synchronised oncoming vehicle, checking that no collision occurs.

requirements.text: In case the radar and camera modules form part of a DCAS approved under R171, the system shall be designed to guard against reasonably foreseeable misuse by the driver.
requirements.test_case: Review the misuse analysis in the Annex 3 safety concept and test identified misuse cases on the vehicle.

requirements.text: In case the radar and camera modules form part of a DCAS, if the system detects a risk of collision, it shall aim to avoid or mitigate the severity of the collision.
requirements.test_case: Run Annex 4 collision-risk scenarios (e.g. decelerating or stationary lead vehicle) and check for avoidance or mitigation.

requirements.text: In case the radar and camera modules form part of a DCAS, the system shall control the longitudinal and lateral motion of the vehicle aiming to maintain appropriate distances from other road users.
requirements.test_case: Measure following and lateral distances to target vehicles in Annex 4 scenarios.

requirements.text: In case the radar and camera modules form part of a DCAS, when the system identifies that the vehicle is approaching a system boundary of a feature in 'active' mode, it shall inform the driver with sufficient lead time for the driver to respond appropriately.
requirements.test_case: Drive towards declared boundaries (e.g. missing lane markings) and measure the lead time of the driver notification.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS provides positioning in the lane of travel, the system in 'active' mode shall assist in keeping the vehicle in a stable position within its lane of travel.
requirements.test_case: Perform the Annex 4 lane-keeping tests and evaluate lateral position stability.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS provides positioning in the lane of travel, while in 'active' mode the system shall ensure that the vehicle does not leave its lane of travel for the lateral acceleration values specified by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Drive curves up to the declared lateral acceleration and check that no lane marking is crossed.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS provides positioning in the lane of travel, the system shall have the capability to adapt the vehicle speed in response to road curvature.
requirements.test_case: Approach curves of decreasing radius and verify that speed is reduced to keep lateral acceleration within the declared value.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS provides positioning in the lane of travel, the activated feature shall at any time, within the boundary conditions, ensure that the M1 vehicle does not unintentionally cross a lane marking for lateral accelerations up to the manufacturer-specified value, which shall not exceed 3 m/s².
requirements.test_case: Perform Annex 4 lane-keeping tests up to the declared lateral acceleration and check the declared value is ≤ 3 m/s² and no marking is crossed.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS has a manoeuvre feature, a manoeuvre shall not be initiated if a risk of collision with another vehicle or road user is detected in the predicted path of the DCAS vehicle during the manoeuvre.
requirements.test_case: Request a manoeuvre with a target vehicle in the predicted path and verify that no manoeuvre is initiated.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS is capable of system-initiated manoeuvres or of withholding hands-on requests, when the following distance to a vehicle in front is temporarily disrupted, the vehicle shall readjust the following distance at the next available opportunity without harsh braking, unless an emergency manoeuvre becomes necessary.
requirements.test_case: Run cut-in and decelerating lead vehicle scenarios and record the deceleration and gap recovery.

requirements.text: In case the radar and camera modules form part of a DCAS, upon detection of a failure (including sensor blockage or misalignment) affecting the safe operation of a feature or the system, the control assistance of the affected feature(s) or system shall be terminated in a safe manner in accordance with the manufacturer's safety concept.
requirements.test_case: Inject a sensor failure or blockage during active operation and verify safe termination of assistance.

requirements.text: In case the radar and camera modules form part of a DCAS, the system shall gradually reduce the control assistance of the affected feature(s) or system if it is safe to do so, and inform the driver according to paragraph 5.5.4.1.
requirements.test_case: Simulate a radar or camera failure and record the assistance ramp-down and the driver warning.

requirements.text: In case of a DCAS approved under R171: the DCAS or its features shall only enter 'active' mode if the other safety systems according to paragraph 5.2 (e.g. AEBS using the same radar and camera sensors) are functional.
requirements.test_case: Disable or fault the AEBS function (e.g. by simulating a radar fault) and verify that the DCAS cannot be switched into 'active' mode.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS is hands-off capable (HORs withheld): the system shall issue an HOR or DCA, as appropriate, upon reaching the system boundaries because the driver overrides the longitudinal control by accelerating.
requirements.test_case: On a highway in hands-off mode, accelerate beyond the system boundary by accelerator override and verify that an HOR or DCA is issued.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS is hands-off capable and can suppress accelerator input to avoid exceeding the system boundaries: the driver shall be able to override this accelerator suppression.
requirements.test_case: Approach a detected system boundary in hands-off mode, press the accelerator firmly and verify that the vehicle accelerates despite the suppression strategy.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS performs manoeuvres (e.g. lane change assistance): when a driver steering override occurs during a manoeuvre, the manoeuvre shall be terminated unless the steering input supports the intended manoeuvre and/or provides only minor lateral corrections.
requirements.test_case: During a system-performed lane change, apply an opposing steering input and verify that the manoeuvre is terminated.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS navigates around an obstruction in the lane of travel, the system shall perform this manoeuvre only in these circumstances: (a) driving around a stationary obstacle (e.g. parked vehicle, debris) in the lane; (b) passing a very slow-moving vehicle or road user with sufficient lateral distance; or (c) where the manoeuvre is instructed by legitimate external sources (e.g. static and dynamic road signs, road works, emergency or enforcement instruction), if applicable to the system's design. Other reasons are allowed only if the Type Approval Authority accepts them as appropriate and safe.
requirements.test_case: Run Annex 4 obstruction scenarios and check the system starts the manoeuvre only for stationary obstacles, very slow road users or legitimate external instructions.

requirements.text: In case the DCAS is equipped with a lane change feature, the system shall respond within the rear, front and side ranges declared by the manufacturer to each of the following, under the declared conditions: a motorcycle, a blocked target lane, and the types of obstacles declared by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Run the Annex 4 lane change tests with motorcycle targets, a blocked target lane and the declared obstacle types placed at the declared ranges, and check that the system responds.

requirements.text: In case of driver-initiated lane change assistance: the system shall react to another vehicle that starts changing into the same space within the target lane, so as to avoid a potential risk of collision.
requirements.test_case: Track test with a target vehicle merging into the same target-lane space during a driver-initiated lane change, checking that the VUT reacts and no collision risk arises.

requirements.text: In case of driver-confirmed or system-initiated lane changes: the system shall react to another vehicle that starts changing into the same space within the target lane, so as to avoid a potential risk of collision.
requirements.test_case: Track test with a target vehicle merging into the same target-lane space during a system-initiated lane change, checking that the VUT reacts and avoids the collision risk.

requirements.text: The external surface of the vehicle, including the bumper fascia and any exposed bumper, radar or camera parts, shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any pointed or sharp parts or any projections of such shape, dimensions, direction or hardness as to be likely to increase the risk or seriousness of bodily injury to a person hit by or brushing against the external surface in a collision.
requirements.test_case: Visually and tactilely inspect the installed bumper system on the vehicle for outward-directed pointed, sharp or hazardous projections.

requirements.text: The external surface of the vehicle, including the bumper system, shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any part likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the installed bumper for hooks, open edges, gaps or protrusions that could catch clothing or limbs.

requirements.text: No protruding part of the external surface of the bumper system shall have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm, except parts that protrude less than 5 mm.
requirements.test_case: Measure the radii of all protruding edges with radius gauges or a 3D scan and confirm each is at least 2.5 mm where the protrusion is 5 mm or more, determining protrusion per Annex 3.

requirements.text: Parts of the external surface of the bumper system that protrude less than 5 mm but 1.5 mm or more shall have their outward facing angles blunted.
requirements.test_case: Measure the protrusion height of small features and inspect that the outward-facing angles of those protruding 1.5 mm to under 5 mm are blunted.

requirements.text: In case a protruding part of the bumper system's external surface has a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm, it shall be made of a material with a hardness not exceeding 60 Shore A, measured with the component as installed on the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Measure the Shore A hardness on the installed component and confirm it is 60 Shore A or less, or use a comparable method where Shore A is impossible.

requirements.text: In case of an ornament or logo on the bumper: added ornaments which project more than 10 mm from their support (including any base on which the ornament is mounted) shall retract, become detached or bend over under a force of 10 daN exerted at their most salient point in any direction in a plane approximately parallel to the surface on which they are mounted.
requirements.test_case: Apply 10 daN with a flat-ended ram of not more than 50 mm diameter at the most salient point of the ornament in several in-plane directions and check that it retracts, detaches or bends over.

requirements.text: In case of an ornament mounted on a radiator grille integrated in the bumper: the ornament shall meet the general requirements of paragraph 5 instead of the 10 daN retraction requirement.
requirements.test_case: Measure the projection and radii of the grille ornament against paragraph 5 limits.

requirements.text: In case of an ornament on the bumper: after the ornament is retracted, detached or bent over, the remaining projections shall not project more than 10 mm.
requirements.test_case: Measure the remaining projection after the 10 daN force test using the Annex 3 method.

requirements.text: In case of an ornament on the bumper: the projections remaining after the ornament is retracted, detached or bent over shall in any case satisfy the provisions of paragraph 5.2.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the remaining parts after the force test for pointed, sharp or dangerous projections per paragraph 5.2.

requirements.text: Protective strips or shielding on the external surface of the bumper shall be firmly secured to the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the fixings and apply a manual pull or push to the strips to confirm they are firmly secured.

requirements.text: In case of grille or air-intake openings in the fascia: for the gaps to be exempt from paragraph 5.4, the distance between consecutive fixed or movable elements shall not exceed 40 mm and the grilles and gaps shall have a functional purpose.
requirements.test_case: Measure the distance between consecutive grille elements according to Annex 3 paragraph 4 and review the functional purpose of each opening.

requirements.text: In case of grille or air-intake openings in the fascia: for gaps between 40 mm and 25 mm between consecutive elements, the radii of curvature of the elements shall be 1 mm or more.
requirements.test_case: Measure the gap per Annex 3 paragraph 4 and check the element edge radii with radius gauges.

requirements.text: In case of grille or air-intake openings in the fascia: if the distance between two consecutive elements is equal to or less than 25 mm, the radii of curvature of the external faces of the elements shall not be less than 0.5 mm.
requirements.test_case: Check the external face radii of the grille elements with radius gauges or a profile scan.

requirements.text: In case of grille or air-intake openings in the fascia: the junction of the front with the side faces of each element forming a grille or gap shall be blunted.
requirements.test_case: Visually and tactilely inspect each grille element edge for blunting.

requirements.text: The ends of the bumper shall be turned in towards the external surface in order to minimize the risk of fouling.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the bumper ends on the vehicle for their turn-in towards the bodywork.

requirements.text: The bumper end turn-in requirement is satisfied if either the bumper is recessed or integrated within the bodywork, or the end of the bumper is turned in so that it is not contactable by a 100 mm sphere and the gap between the bumper end and the surrounding bodywork does not exceed 20 mm.
requirements.test_case: Apply a 100 mm sphere to the bumper ends and measure the bumper-to-body gap with a gap gauge (at most 20 mm).

requirements.text: If the line of the bumper which corresponds to the outline contour of the car vertical projection is on a rigid surface, that surface shall have a minimum radius of curvature of 5 mm at all its points lying from the contour line to 20 mm inward, within the zone between and in front of the tangential points with the contour line of two vertical planes each at 15° to the vehicle longitudinal plane of symmetry.
